1572|
1573|        fieldsets = self.get_fieldsets(request, obj)
1574|        ModelForm = self.get_form(
1575|            request, obj, change=not add, fields=flatten_fieldsets(fieldsets)
1576|        )
1577|        if request.method == 'POST':
1578|            form = ModelForm(request.POST, request.FILES, instance=obj)
1579|            form_validated = form.is_valid()
1580|            if form_validated:
1581|                new_object = self.save_form(request, form, change=not add)
1582|            else:
1583|                new_object = form.instance
1584|            formsets, inline_instances = self._create_formsets(request, new_object, change=not add)
1585|            if all_valid(formsets) and form_validated:
1586|                self.save_model(request, new_object, form, not add)
1587|                self.save_related(request, form, formsets, not add)
1588|                change_message = self.construct_change_message(request, form, formsets, add)
1589|                if add:
1590|                    self.log_addition(request, new_object, change_message)
1591|                    return self.response_add(request, new_object)
1592|                else:
1593|                    self.log_change(request, new_object, change_message)
1594|                    return self.response_change(request, new_object)
1595|            else:
1596|                form_validated = False
1597|        else:
1598|            if add:
1599|                initial = self.get_changeform_initial_data(request)
1600|                form = ModelForm(initial=initial)
1601|                formsets, inline_instances = self._create_formsets(request, form.instance, change=False)
1602|            else:
1603|                form = ModelForm(instance=obj)
1604|                formsets, inline_instances = self._create_formsets(request, obj, change=True)
1605|
1606|        if not add and not self.has_change_permission(request, obj):
1607|            readonly_fields = flatten_fieldsets(fieldsets)
1608|        else:
1609|            readonly_fields = self.get_readonly_fields(request, obj)
1610|        adminForm = helpers.AdminForm(
1611|            form,
1612|            list(fieldsets),
1613|            # Clear prepopulated fields on a view-only form to avoid a crash.
1614|            self.get_prepopulated_fields(request, obj) if add or self.has_change_permission(request, obj) else {},
1615|            readonly_fields,
1616|            model_admin=self)
1617|        media = self.media + adminForm.media
1618|
1619|        inline_formsets = self.get_inline_formsets(request, formsets, inline_instances, obj)
1620|        for inline_formset in inline_formsets:
1621|            media = media + inline_formset.media
1622|
1623|        if add:
1624|            title = _('Add %s')
1625|        elif self.has_change_permission(request, obj):

1627|        else:
1628|            title = _('View %s')
1629|        context = {
1630|            **self.admin_site.each_context(request),
1631|            'title': title % opts.verbose_name,
1632|            'subtitle': str(obj) if obj else None,
1633|            'adminform': adminForm,
1634|            'object_id': object_id,

1638|            'media': media,

1640|            'errors': helpers.AdminErrorList(form, formsets),
1641|            'preserved_filters': self.get_preserved_filters(request),

1736|                helpers.ACTION_CHECKBOX_NAME in request.POST and
1737|                'index' not in request.POST and '_save' not in request.POST):
1738|            if selected:

1740|                if response:

1742|                else:
1743|                    action_failed = True
1744|

### GitHub Problem Description ###
Log exceptions handled in Signal.send_robust()
Description
	
As pointed out by ​Haki Benita on Twitter, by default Signal.send_robust() doesn't have any log messages for exceptions raised in receivers. Since Django logs exceptions in other similar situations, such as missing template variables, I think it would be worth adding a logger.exception() call in the except clause of send_robust() . Users would then see such exceptions in their error handling tools, e.g. Sentry, and be able to figure out what action to take from there. Ultimately any *expected* exception should be caught with a try in the receiver function.

### GitHub Problem Description ###
Abstract model field should not be equal across models
Description
	
Consider the following models:
class A(models.Model):
	class Meta:
		abstract = True
	myfield = IntegerField()
class B(A):
	pass
class C(A):
	pass
If I pull the fields of B and C into a shared set, one will be de-duplicated away, because they compare as equal. I found this surprising, though in practice using a list was sufficient for my need. The root of the issue is that they compare equal, as fields only consider self.creation_counter when comparing for equality.
len({B._meta.get_field('myfield'), C._meta.get_field('myfield')}) == 1
B._meta.get_field('myfield') == C._meta.get_field('myfield')
We should adjust __eq__ so that if the field.model is different, they will compare unequal. Similarly, it is probably wise to adjust __hash__ and __lt__ to match.
When adjusting __lt__, it may be wise to order first by self.creation_counter so that cases not affected by this equality collision won't be re-ordered. In my experimental branch, there was one test that broke if I ordered them by model first.
I brought this up on IRC django-dev to check my intuitions, and those conversing with me there seemed to agree that the current behavior is not intuitive.

### GitHub Problem Description ###
Upgrading 2.2>3.0 causes named tuples used as arguments to __range to error.
Description
	
I noticed this while upgrading a project from 2.2 to 3.0.
This project passes named 2-tuples as arguments to range queryset filters. This works fine on 2.2. On 3.0 it causes the following error: TypeError: __new__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'far'.
This happens because django.db.models.sql.query.Query.resolve_lookup_value goes into the tuple elements to resolve lookups and then attempts to reconstitute the tuple with the resolved elements.
When it attempts to construct the new tuple it preserves the type (the named tuple) but it passes a iterator to it's constructor.
NamedTuples don't have the code path for copying an iterator, and so it errors on insufficient arguments.
The fix is to * expand the contents of the iterator into the constructor.

1025|    def _get_unique_checks(self, exclude=None):
1026|        """

1028|        called from a ModelForm, some fields may have been excluded; we can't
1029|        perform a unique check on a model that is missing fields involved
1030|        in that check. Fields that did not validate should also be excluded,
1031|        but they need to be passed in via the exclude argument.
1032|        """
1033|        if exclude is None:
1034|            exclude = []
1035|        unique_checks = []
1036|
1037|        unique_togethers = [(self.__class__, self._meta.unique_together)]
1038|        constraints = [(self.__class__, self._meta.total_unique_constraints)]
1039|        for parent_class in self._meta.get_parent_list():
1040|            if parent_class._meta.unique_together:
1041|                unique_togethers.append((parent_class, parent_class._meta.unique_together))
1042|            if parent_class._meta.total_unique_constraints:
1043|                constraints.append(
1044|                    (parent_class, parent_class._meta.total_unique_constraints)
1045|                )
1046|
1047|        for model_class, unique_together in unique_togethers:
1048|            for check in unique_together:
1049|                if not any(name in exclude for name in check):
1050|                    # Add the check if the field isn't excluded.
1051|                    unique_checks.append((model_class, tuple(check)))
1052|
1053|        for model_class, model_constraints in constraints:
1054|            for constraint in model_constraints:
1055|                if not any(name in exclude for name in constraint.fields):
1056|                    unique_checks.append((model_class, constraint.fields))
1057|
1058|        # These are checks for the unique_for_<date/year/month>.
1059|        date_checks = []
1060|
1061|        # Gather a list of checks for fields declared as unique and add them to
1062|        # the list of checks.
1063|
1064|        fields_with_class = [(self.__class__, self._meta.local_fields)]
1065|        for parent_class in self._meta.get_parent_list():
1066|            fields_with_class.append((parent_class, parent_class._meta.local_fields))
1067|
1068|        for model_class, fields in fields_with_class:
1069|            for f in fields:
1070|                name = f.name
1071|                if name in exclude:
1072|                    continue
1073|                if f.unique:
1074|                    unique_checks.append((model_class, (name,)))
1075|                if f.unique_for_date and f.unique_for_date not in exclude:
1076|                    date_checks.append((model_class, 'date', name, f.unique_for_date))
1077|                if f.unique_for_year and f.unique_for_year not in exclude:
1078|                    date_checks.append((model_class, 'year', name, f.unique_for_year))
1079|                if f.unique_for_month and f.unique_for_month not in exclude:
1080|                    date_checks.append((model_class, 'month', name, f.unique_for_month))
1081|        return unique_checks, date_checks

1084|        errors = {}

1088|            # object's values for all the unique field.

1095|                if (lookup_value is None or
1096|                        (lookup_value == '' and connection.features.interprets_empty_strings_as_nulls)):
1097|                    # no value, skip the lookup
1098|                    continue
1099|                if f.primary_key and not self._state.adding:
1100|                    # no need to check for unique primary key when editing
1101|                    continue

1103|

1105|            if len(unique_check) != len(lookup_kwargs):

Please review the following GitHub problem description and relevant files, and provide a set of locations that need to be edited to fix the issue.
The locations can be specified as class names, function or method names, or exact line numbers that require modification.

### GitHub Problem Description ###
Saving parent object after setting on child leads to data loss for parents with non-numeric primary key.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Charlie DeTar)
	 
Given a model with a foreign key relation to another model that has a non-auto CharField as its primary key:
class Product(models.Model):
	sku = models.CharField(primary_key=True, max_length=50)
class Order(models.Model):
	product = models.ForeignKey(Product, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
If the relation is initialized on the parent with an empty instance that does not yet specify its primary key, and the primary key is subsequently defined, the parent does not "see" the primary key's change:
with transaction.atomic():
	order = Order()
	order.product = Product()
	order.product.sku = "foo"
	order.product.save()
	order.save()
	assert Order.objects.filter(product_id="").exists() # Succeeds, but shouldn't
	assert Order.objects.filter(product=order.product).exists() # Fails
Instead of product_id being populated with product.sku, it is set to emptystring. The foreign key constraint which would enforce the existence of a product with sku="" is deferred until the transaction commits. The transaction does correctly fail on commit with a ForeignKeyViolation due to the non-existence of a product with emptystring as its primary key.
On the other hand, if the related unsaved instance is initialized with its primary key before assignment to the parent, it is persisted correctly:
with transaction.atomic():
	order = Order()
	order.product = Product(sku="foo")
	order.product.save()
	order.save()
	assert Order.objects.filter(product=order.product).exists() # succeeds
Committing the transaction also succeeds.
This may have something to do with how the Order.product_id field is handled at assignment, together with something about handling fetching of auto vs non-auto primary keys from the related instance.

604|        all non-deferred fields are reloaded.

613|            for field in fields:

615|                    del prefetched_objects_cache[field]

622|                    'are not allowed in fields.' % LOOKUP_SEP)

628|        deferred_fields = self.get_deferred_fields()

644|            # Clear cached foreign keys.

874|    def _do_update(self, base_qs, using, pk_val, values, update_fields, forced_update):

882|            # update_fields doesn't target any field in current model. In that
883|            # case we just say the update succeeded. Another case ending up here
884|            # is a model with just PK - in that case check that the PK still
885|            # exists.
886|            return update_fields is not None or filtered.exists()
887|        if self._meta.select_on_save and not forced_update:
888|            return (
889|                filtered.exists() and
890|                # It may happen that the object is deleted from the DB right after
891|                # this check, causing the subsequent UPDATE to return zero matching
892|                # rows. The same result can occur in some rare cases when the
893|                # database returns zero despite the UPDATE being executed

895|                # distinguish these two cases, the object's existence in the
896|                # database is again checked for if the UPDATE query returns 0.
897|                (filtered._update(values) > 0 or filtered.exists())

1025|    def _get_unique_checks(self, exclude=None):

1028|        called from a ModelForm, some fields may have been excluded; we can't
1029|        perform a unique check on a model that is missing fields involved
1030|        in that check. Fields that did not validate should also be excluded,
1031|        but they need to be passed in via the exclude argument.
1032|        """
1033|        if exclude is None:
1034|            exclude = []

1037|        unique_togethers = [(self.__class__, self._meta.unique_together)]
1038|        constraints = [(self.__class__, self._meta.total_unique_constraints)]
1039|        for parent_class in self._meta.get_parent_list():
1040|            if parent_class._meta.unique_together:
1041|                unique_togethers.append((parent_class, parent_class._meta.unique_together))
1042|            if parent_class._meta.total_unique_constraints:
1043|                constraints.append(
1044|                    (parent_class, parent_class._meta.total_unique_constraints)
1045|                )
1046|
1047|        for model_class, unique_together in unique_togethers:
1048|            for check in unique_together:
1049|                if not any(name in exclude for name in check):
1050|                    # Add the check if the field isn't excluded.
1051|                    unique_checks.append((model_class, tuple(check)))
1052|
1053|        for model_class, model_constraints in constraints:
1054|            for constraint in model_constraints:
1055|                if not any(name in exclude for name in constraint.fields):
1056|                    unique_checks.append((model_class, constraint.fields))
1057|
1058|        # These are checks for the unique_for_<date/year/month>.
1059|        date_checks = []
1060|
1061|        # Gather a list of checks for fields declared as unique and add them to
1062|        # the list of checks.
1063|
1064|        fields_with_class = [(self.__class__, self._meta.local_fields)]
1065|        for parent_class in self._meta.get_parent_list():
1066|            fields_with_class.append((parent_class, parent_class._meta.local_fields))
1067|
1068|        for model_class, fields in fields_with_class:
1069|            for f in fields:
1070|                name = f.name
1071|                if name in exclude:
1072|                    continue
1073|                if f.unique:
1074|                    unique_checks.append((model_class, (name,)))
1075|                if f.unique_for_date and f.unique_for_date not in exclude:
1076|                    date_checks.append((model_class, 'date', name, f.unique_for_date))
1077|                if f.unique_for_year and f.unique_for_year not in exclude:
1078|                    date_checks.append((model_class, 'year', name, f.unique_for_year))
1079|                if f.unique_for_month and f.unique_for_month not in exclude:
1080|                    date_checks.append((model_class, 'month', name, f.unique_for_month))

### GitHub Problem Description ###
BoundWidget.id_for_label ignores id set by ChoiceWidget.options
Description
	
If you look at the implementation of BoundField.subwidgets
class BoundField:
	...
	def subwidgets(self):
		id_ = self.field.widget.attrs.get('id') or self.auto_id
		attrs = {'id': id_} if id_ else {}
		attrs = self.build_widget_attrs(attrs)
		return [
			BoundWidget(self.field.widget, widget, self.form.renderer)
			for widget in self.field.widget.subwidgets(self.html_name, self.value(), attrs=attrs)
		]
one sees that self.field.widget.subwidgets(self.html_name, self.value(), attrs=attrs) returns a dict and assigns it to widget. Now widget['attrs']['id'] contains the "id" we would like to use when rendering the label of our CheckboxSelectMultiple.
However BoundWidget.id_for_label() is implemented as
class BoundWidget:
	...
	def id_for_label(self):
		return 'id_%s_%s' % (self.data['name'], self.data['index'])
ignoring the id available through self.data['attrs']['id']. This re-implementation for rendering the "id" is confusing and presumably not intended. Nobody has probably realized that so far, because rarely the auto_id-argument is overridden when initializing a form. If however we do, one would assume that the method BoundWidget.id_for_label renders that string as specified through the auto_id format-string.
By changing the code from above to
class BoundWidget:
	...
	def id_for_label(self):
		return self.data['attrs']['id']
that function behaves as expected.
Please note that this error only occurs when rendering the subwidgets of a widget of type CheckboxSelectMultiple. This has nothing to do with the method BoundField.id_for_label().

451|            if (

462|    def generate_renamed_models(self):
463|        """
464|        Find any renamed models, generate the operations for them, and remove
465|        the old entry from the model lists. Must be run before other
466|        model-level generation.
467|        """
468|        self.renamed_models = {}
469|        self.renamed_models_rel = {}

471|        for app_label, model_name in sorted(added_models):
472|            model_state = self.to_state.models[app_label, model_name]
473|            model_fields_def = self.only_relation_agnostic_fields(model_state.fields)
474|
475|            removed_models = self.old_model_keys - self.new_model_keys
476|            for rem_app_label, rem_model_name in removed_models:
477|                if rem_app_label == app_label:
478|                    rem_model_state = self.from_state.models[rem_app_label, rem_model_name]
479|                    rem_model_fields_def = self.only_relation_agnostic_fields(rem_model_state.fields)
480|                    if model_fields_def == rem_model_fields_def:
481|                        if self.questioner.ask_rename_model(rem_model_state, model_state):
482|                            dependencies = []
483|                            fields = list(model_state.fields.values()) + [
484|                                field.remote_field
485|                                for relations in self.to_state.relations[app_label, model_name].values()
486|                                for _, field in relations
487|                            ]
488|                            for field in fields:
489|                                if field.is_relation:
490|                                    dependencies.extend(
491|                                        self._get_dependencies_for_foreign_key(
492|                                            app_label, model_name, field, self.to_state,
493|                                        )
494|                                    )
495|                            self.add_operation(
496|                                app_label,
497|                                operations.RenameModel(
498|                                    old_name=rem_model_state.name,
499|                                    new_name=model_state.name,
500|                                ),
501|                                dependencies=dependencies,
502|                            )
503|                            self.renamed_models[app_label, model_name] = rem_model_name
504|                            renamed_models_rel_key = '%s.%s' % (
505|                                rem_model_state.app_label,
506|                                rem_model_state.name_lower,
507|                            )
508|                            self.renamed_models_rel[renamed_models_rel_key] = '%s.%s' % (
509|                                model_state.app_label,
510|                                model_state.name_lower,
511|                            )
512|                            self.old_model_keys.remove((rem_app_label, rem_model_name))
513|                            self.old_model_keys.add((app_label, model_name))
514|                            break

516|    def generate_created_models(self):
517|        """
518|        Find all new models (both managed and unmanaged) and make create
519|        operations for them as well as separate operations to create any
520|        foreign key or M2M relationships (these are optimized later, if
521|        possible).
522|
523|        Defer any model options that refer to collections of fields that might
524|        be deferred (e.g. unique_together, index_together).
525|        """
526|        old_keys = self.old_model_keys | self.old_unmanaged_keys
527|        added_models = self.new_model_keys - old_keys
528|        added_unmanaged_models = self.new_unmanaged_keys - old_keys
529|        all_added_models = chain(
530|            sorted(added_models, key=self.swappable_first_key, reverse=True),
531|            sorted(added_unmanaged_models, key=self.swappable_first_key, reverse=True)
532|        )
533|        for app_label, model_name in all_added_models:
534|            model_state = self.to_state.models[app_label, model_name]
535|            # Gather related fields
536|            related_fields = {}
537|            primary_key_rel = None
538|            for field_name, field in model_state.fields.items():
539|                if field.remote_field:
540|                    if field.remote_field.model:
541|                        if field.primary_key:
542|                            primary_key_rel = field.remote_field.model
543|                        elif not field.remote_field.parent_link:
544|                            related_fields[field_name] = field
545|                    if getattr(field.remote_field, 'through', None):
546|                        related_fields[field_name] = field
547|
548|            # Are there indexes/unique|index_together to defer?
549|            indexes = model_state.options.pop('indexes')
550|            constraints = model_state.options.pop('constraints')
551|            unique_together = model_state.options.pop('unique_together', None)
552|            index_together = model_state.options.pop('index_together', None)
553|            order_with_respect_to = model_state.options.pop('order_with_respect_to', None)
554|            # Depend on the deletion of any possible proxy version of us
555|            dependencies = [
556|                (app_label, model_name, None, False),
557|            ]
558|            # Depend on all bases
559|            for base in model_state.bases:
560|                if isinstance(base, str) and "." in base:
561|                    base_app_label, base_name = base.split(".", 1)
562|                    dependencies.append((base_app_label, base_name, None, True))
563|                    # Depend on the removal of base fields if the new model has
564|                    # a field with the same name.
565|                    old_base_model_state = self.from_state.models.get((base_app_label, base_name))
566|                    new_base_model_state = self.to_state.models.get((base_app_label, base_name))
567|                    if old_base_model_state and new_base_model_state:
568|                        removed_base_fields = set(old_base_model_state.fields).difference(
569|                            new_base_model_state.fields,
570|                        ).intersection(model_state.fields)
571|                        for removed_base_field in removed_base_fields:
572|                            dependencies.append((base_app_label, base_name, removed_base_field, False))
573|            # Depend on the other end of the primary key if it's a relation
574|            if primary_key_rel:
575|                dependencies.append(
576|                    resolve_relation(
577|                        primary_key_rel, app_label, model_name,
578|                    ) + (None, True)
579|                )
580|            # Generate creation operation
581|            self.add_operation(
582|                app_label,
583|                operations.CreateModel(
584|                    name=model_state.name,
585|                    fields=[d for d in model_state.fields.items() if d[0] not in related_fields],
586|                    options=model_state.options,
587|                    bases=model_state.bases,
588|                    managers=model_state.managers,
589|                ),
590|                dependencies=dependencies,
591|                beginning=True,
592|            )
593|
594|            # Don't add operations which modify the database for unmanaged models
595|            if not model_state.options.get('managed', True):
596|                continue
597|
598|            # Generate operations for each related field
599|            for name, field in sorted(related_fields.items()):
600|                dependencies = self._get_dependencies_for_foreign_key(
601|                    app_label, model_name, field, self.to_state,
602|                )
603|                # Depend on our own model being created
604|                dependencies.append((app_label, model_name, None, True))
605|                # Make operation
606|                self.add_operation(
607|                    app_label,
608|                    operations.AddField(
609|                        model_name=model_name,
610|                        name=name,
611|                        field=field,
612|                    ),
613|                    dependencies=list(set(dependencies)),
614|                )
615|            # Generate other opns
616|            if order_with_respect_to:
617|                self.add_operation(
618|                    app_label,
619|                    operations.AlterOrderWithRespectTo(
620|                        name=model_name,
621|                        order_with_respect_to=order_with_respect_to,
622|                    ),
623|                    dependencies=[
624|                        (app_label, model_name, order_with_respect_to, True),
625|                        (app_label, model_name, None, True),
626|                    ]
627|                )
628|            related_dependencies = [
629|                (app_label, model_name, name, True)
630|                for name in sorted(related_fields)
631|            ]
632|            related_dependencies.append((app_label, model_name, None, True))
633|            for index in indexes:
634|                self.add_operation(
635|                    app_label,
636|                    operations.AddIndex(
637|                        model_name=model_name,
638|                        index=index,
639|                    ),
640|                    dependencies=related_dependencies,
641|                )
642|            for constraint in constraints:
643|                self.add_operation(
644|                    app_label,
645|                    operations.AddConstraint(
646|                        model_name=model_name,
647|                        constraint=constraint,
648|                    ),
649|                    dependencies=related_dependencies,
650|                )
651|            if unique_together:
652|                self.add_operation(
653|                    app_label,
654|                    operations.AlterUniqueTogether(
655|                        name=model_name,
656|                        unique_together=unique_together,
657|                    ),
658|                    dependencies=related_dependencies
659|                )
660|            if index_together:
661|                self.add_operation(
662|                    app_label,
663|                    operations.AlterIndexTogether(
664|                        name=model_name,
665|                        index_together=index_together,
666|                    ),
667|                    dependencies=related_dependencies
668|                )
669|            # Fix relationships if the model changed from a proxy model to a
670|            # concrete model.
671|            relations = self.to_state.relations
672|            if (app_label, model_name) in self.old_proxy_keys:
673|                for related_model_key, related_fields in relations[app_label, model_name].items():
674|                    related_model_state = self.to_state.models[related_model_key]
675|                    for related_field_name, related_field in related_fields:
676|                        self.add_operation(
677|                            related_model_state.app_label,
678|                            operations.AlterField(
679|                                model_name=related_model_state.name,
680|                                name=related_field_name,
681|                                field=related_field,
682|                            ),
683|                            dependencies=[(app_label, model_name, None, True)],
684|                        )

719|    def generate_deleted_models(self):
720|        """
721|        Find all deleted models (managed and unmanaged) and make delete
722|        operations for them as well as separate operations to delete any
723|        foreign key or M2M relationships (these are optimized later, if
724|        possible).
725|
726|        Also bring forward removal of any model options that refer to
727|        collections of fields - the inverse of generate_created_models().
728|        """
729|        new_keys = self.new_model_keys | self.new_unmanaged_keys
730|        deleted_models = self.old_model_keys - new_keys
731|        deleted_unmanaged_models = self.old_unmanaged_keys - new_keys
732|        all_deleted_models = chain(sorted(deleted_models), sorted(deleted_unmanaged_models))
733|        for app_label, model_name in all_deleted_models:
734|            model_state = self.from_state.models[app_label, model_name]
735|            # Gather related fields
736|            related_fields = {}
737|            for field_name, field in model_state.fields.items():
738|                if field.remote_field:
739|                    if field.remote_field.model:
740|                        related_fields[field_name] = field
741|                    if getattr(field.remote_field, 'through', None):
742|                        related_fields[field_name] = field
743|            # Generate option removal first
744|            unique_together = model_state.options.pop('unique_together', None)
745|            index_together = model_state.options.pop('index_together', None)
746|            if unique_together:
747|                self.add_operation(
748|                    app_label,
749|                    operations.AlterUniqueTogether(
750|                        name=model_name,
751|                        unique_together=None,
752|                    )
753|                )
754|            if index_together:
755|                self.add_operation(
756|                    app_label,
757|                    operations.AlterIndexTogether(
758|                        name=model_name,
759|                        index_together=None,
760|                    )
761|                )
762|            # Then remove each related field
763|            for name in sorted(related_fields):
764|                self.add_operation(
765|                    app_label,
766|                    operations.RemoveField(
767|                        model_name=model_name,
768|                        name=name,
769|                    )
770|                )
771|            # Finally, remove the model.
772|            # This depends on both the removal/alteration of all incoming fields
773|            # and the removal of all its own related fields, and if it's
774|            # a through model the field that references it.
775|            dependencies = []
776|            relations = self.from_state.relations
777|            for (related_object_app_label, object_name), relation_related_fields in (
778|                relations[app_label, model_name].items()
779|            ):
780|                for field_name, field in relation_related_fields:
781|                    dependencies.append(
782|                        (related_object_app_label, object_name, field_name, False),
783|                    )
784|                    if not field.many_to_many:
785|                        dependencies.append(
786|                            (related_object_app_label, object_name, field_name, 'alter'),
787|                        )
788|
789|            for name in sorted(related_fields):
790|                dependencies.append((app_label, model_name, name, False))
791|            # We're referenced in another field's through=
792|            through_user = self.through_users.get((app_label, model_state.name_lower))
793|            if through_user:
794|                dependencies.append((through_user[0], through_user[1], through_user[2], False))
795|            # Finally, make the operation, deduping any dependencies
796|            self.add_operation(
797|                app_label,
798|                operations.DeleteModel(
799|                    name=model_state.name,
800|                ),
801|                dependencies=list(set(dependencies)),
802|            )

817|    def generate_renamed_fields(self):
818|        """Work out renamed fields."""
819|        self.renamed_fields = {}
820|        for app_label, model_name, field_name in sorted(self.new_field_keys - self.old_field_keys):
821|            old_model_name = self.renamed_models.get((app_label, model_name), model_name)
822|            old_model_state = self.from_state.models[app_label, old_model_name]
823|            new_model_state = self.to_state.models[app_label, old_model_name]
824|            field = new_model_state.get_field(field_name)
825|            # Scan to see if this is actually a rename!
826|            field_dec = self.deep_deconstruct(field)
827|            for rem_app_label, rem_model_name, rem_field_name in sorted(self.old_field_keys - self.new_field_keys):
828|                if rem_app_label == app_label and rem_model_name == model_name:
829|                    old_field = old_model_state.get_field(rem_field_name)
830|                    old_field_dec = self.deep_deconstruct(old_field)
831|                    if field.remote_field and field.remote_field.model and 'to' in old_field_dec[2]:
832|                        old_rel_to = old_field_dec[2]['to']
833|                        if old_rel_to in self.renamed_models_rel:
834|                            old_field_dec[2]['to'] = self.renamed_models_rel[old_rel_to]
835|                    old_field.set_attributes_from_name(rem_field_name)
836|                    old_db_column = old_field.get_attname_column()[1]
837|                    if (old_field_dec == field_dec or (
838|                            # Was the field renamed and db_column equal to the
839|                            # old field's column added?
840|                            old_field_dec[0:2] == field_dec[0:2] and
841|                            dict(old_field_dec[2], db_column=old_db_column) == field_dec[2])):
842|                        if self.questioner.ask_rename(model_name, rem_field_name, field_name, field):
843|                            self.add_operation(
844|                                app_label,
845|                                operations.RenameField(
846|                                    model_name=model_name,
847|                                    old_name=rem_field_name,
848|                                    new_name=field_name,
849|                                )
850|                            )
851|                            self.old_field_keys.remove((rem_app_label, rem_model_name, rem_field_name))
852|                            self.old_field_keys.add((app_label, model_name, field_name))

861|    def _generate_added_field(self, app_label, model_name, field_name):
862|        field = self.to_state.models[app_label, model_name].get_field(field_name)
863|        # Fields that are foreignkeys/m2ms depend on stuff
864|        dependencies = []
865|        if field.remote_field and field.remote_field.model:
866|            dependencies.extend(self._get_dependencies_for_foreign_key(
867|                app_label, model_name, field, self.to_state,
868|            ))
869|        # You can't just add NOT NULL fields with no default or fields
870|        # which don't allow empty strings as default.
871|        time_fields = (models.DateField, models.DateTimeField, models.TimeField)
872|        preserve_default = (
873|            field.null or field.has_default() or field.many_to_many or
874|            (field.blank and field.empty_strings_allowed) or
875|            (isinstance(field, time_fields) and field.auto_now)
876|        )
877|        if not preserve_default:
878|            field = field.clone()
879|            if isinstance(field, time_fields) and field.auto_now_add:
880|                field.default = self.questioner.ask_auto_now_add_addition(field_name, model_name)
881|            else:
882|                field.default = self.questioner.ask_not_null_addition(field_name, model_name)
883|        self.add_operation(
884|            app_label,
885|            operations.AddField(
886|                model_name=model_name,
887|                name=field_name,
888|                field=field,
889|                preserve_default=preserve_default,
890|            ),
891|            dependencies=dependencies,
892|        )

899|    def _generate_removed_field(self, app_label, model_name, field_name):
900|        self.add_operation(
901|            app_label,
902|            operations.RemoveField(
903|                model_name=model_name,
904|                name=field_name,
905|            ),
906|            # We might need to depend on the removal of an
907|            # order_with_respect_to or index/unique_together operation;
908|            # this is safely ignored if there isn't one
909|            dependencies=[
910|                (app_label, model_name, field_name, "order_wrt_unset"),
911|                (app_label, model_name, field_name, "foo_together_change"),
912|            ],
913|        )

915|    def generate_altered_fields(self):
916|        """
917|        Make AlterField operations, or possibly RemovedField/AddField if alter
918|        isn't possible.
919|        """
920|        for app_label, model_name, field_name in sorted(self.old_field_keys & self.new_field_keys):
921|            # Did the field change?
922|            old_model_name = self.renamed_models.get((app_label, model_name), model_name)
923|            old_field_name = self.renamed_fields.get((app_label, model_name, field_name), field_name)
924|            old_field = self.from_state.models[app_label, old_model_name].get_field(old_field_name)
925|            new_field = self.to_state.models[app_label, model_name].get_field(field_name)
926|            dependencies = []
927|            # Implement any model renames on relations; these are handled by RenameModel
928|            # so we need to exclude them from the comparison
929|            if hasattr(new_field, "remote_field") and getattr(new_field.remote_field, "model", None):
930|                rename_key = resolve_relation(new_field.remote_field.model, app_label, model_name)
931|                if rename_key in self.renamed_models:
932|                    new_field.remote_field.model = old_field.remote_field.model
933|                # Handle ForeignKey which can only have a single to_field.
934|                remote_field_name = getattr(new_field.remote_field, 'field_name', None)
935|                if remote_field_name:
936|                    to_field_rename_key = rename_key + (remote_field_name,)
937|                    if to_field_rename_key in self.renamed_fields:
938|                        # Repoint both model and field name because to_field
939|                        # inclusion in ForeignKey.deconstruct() is based on
940|                        # both.
941|                        new_field.remote_field.model = old_field.remote_field.model
942|                        new_field.remote_field.field_name = old_field.remote_field.field_name
943|                # Handle ForeignObjects which can have multiple from_fields/to_fields.
944|                from_fields = getattr(new_field, 'from_fields', None)
945|                if from_fields:
946|                    from_rename_key = (app_label, model_name)
947|                    new_field.from_fields = tuple([
948|                        self.renamed_fields.get(from_rename_key + (from_field,), from_field)
949|                        for from_field in from_fields
950|                    ])
951|                    new_field.to_fields = tuple([
952|                        self.renamed_fields.get(rename_key + (to_field,), to_field)
953|                        for to_field in new_field.to_fields
954|                    ])
955|                dependencies.extend(self._get_dependencies_for_foreign_key(
956|                    app_label, model_name, new_field, self.to_state,
957|                ))
958|            if (
959|                hasattr(new_field, 'remote_field') and
960|                getattr(new_field.remote_field, 'through', None)
961|            ):
962|                rename_key = resolve_relation(new_field.remote_field.through, app_label, model_name)
963|                if rename_key in self.renamed_models:
964|                    new_field.remote_field.through = old_field.remote_field.through
965|            old_field_dec = self.deep_deconstruct(old_field)
966|            new_field_dec = self.deep_deconstruct(new_field)
967|            if old_field_dec != new_field_dec:
968|                both_m2m = old_field.many_to_many and new_field.many_to_many
969|                neither_m2m = not old_field.many_to_many and not new_field.many_to_many
970|                if both_m2m or neither_m2m:
971|                    # Either both fields are m2m or neither is
972|                    preserve_default = True
973|                    if (old_field.null and not new_field.null and not new_field.has_default() and

### GitHub Problem Description ###
Refactor AutocompleteJsonView to support extra fields in autocomplete response
Description
	 
		(last modified by mrts)
	 
Adding data attributes to items in ordinary non-autocomplete foreign key fields that use forms.widgets.Select-based widgets is relatively easy. This enables powerful and dynamic admin site customizations where fields from related models are updated immediately when users change the selected item.
However, adding new attributes to autocomplete field results currently requires extending contrib.admin.views.autocomplete.AutocompleteJsonView and fully overriding the AutocompleteJsonView.get() method. Here's an example:
class MyModelAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin):
	def get_urls(self):
		return [
			path('autocomplete/', CustomAutocompleteJsonView.as_view(admin_site=self.admin_site))
			if url.pattern.match('autocomplete/')
			else url for url in super().get_urls()
		]
class CustomAutocompleteJsonView(AutocompleteJsonView):
	def get(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
		self.term, self.model_admin, self.source_field, to_field_name = self.process_request(request)
		if not self.has_perm(request):
			raise PermissionDenied
		self.object_list = self.get_queryset()
		context = self.get_context_data()
		return JsonResponse({
			'results': [
				{'id': str(getattr(obj, to_field_name)), 'text': str(obj), 'notes': obj.notes} # <-- customization here
				for obj in context['object_list']
			],
			'pagination': {'more': context['page_obj'].has_next()},
		})
The problem with this is that as AutocompleteJsonView.get() keeps evolving, there's quite a lot of maintenance overhead required to catch up.
The solutions is simple, side-effect- and risk-free: adding a result customization extension point to get() by moving the lines that construct the results inside JsonResponse constructor to a separate method. So instead of
		return JsonResponse({
			'results': [
				{'id': str(getattr(obj, to_field_name)), 'text': str(obj)}
				for obj in context['object_list']
			],
			'pagination': {'more': context['page_obj'].has_next()},
		})
there would be
		return JsonResponse({
			'results': [
				self.serialize_result(obj, to_field_name) for obj in context['object_list']
			],
			'pagination': {'more': context['page_obj'].has_next()},
		})
where serialize_result() contains the original object to dictionary conversion code that would be now easy to override:
def serialize_result(self, obj, to_field_name):
	return {'id': str(getattr(obj, to_field_name)), 'text': str(obj)}
The example CustomAutocompleteJsonView from above would now become succinct and maintainable:
class CustomAutocompleteJsonView(AutocompleteJsonView):
	def serialize_result(self, obj, to_field_name):
		return super.serialize_result(obj, to_field_name) | {'notes': obj.notes}
What do you think, is this acceptable? I'm more than happy to provide the patch.

Description

Prevent developers from defining a related_name on symmetrical ManyToManyFields
Description
	
In ManyToManyField, if the symmetrical argument is passed, or if it's a self-referential ManyToMany relationship, the related field on the target model is not created. However, if a developer passes in the related_name not understanding this fact, they may be confused until they find the information about symmetrical relationship. Thus, it is proposed to raise an error when the user defines a ManyToManyField in this condition.

### GitHub Problem Description ###
QuerySet.defer() doesn't clear deferred field when chaining with only().
Description
	
Considering a simple Company model with four fields: id, name, trade_number and country. If we evaluate a queryset containing a .defer() following a .only(), the generated sql query selects unexpected fields. For example: 
Company.objects.only("name").defer("name")
loads all the fields with the following query:
SELECT "company"."id", "company"."name", "company"."trade_number", "company"."country" FROM "company"
and 
Company.objects.only("name").defer("name").defer("country")
also loads all the fields with the same query:
SELECT "company"."id", "company"."name", "company"."trade_number", "company"."country" FROM "company"
In those two cases, i would expect the sql query to be:
SELECT "company"."id" FROM "company"
In the following example, we get the expected behavior:
Company.objects.only("name", "country").defer("name")
only loads "id" and "country" fields with the following query:
SELECT "company"."id", "company"."country" FROM "company"

Hi,
We have a multi-db setup. We have one connection that is for the django project, and several connections that talk to other dbs for information (ie models with managed = False). Django should only create tables in the first connection, never in any of the other connections. We have a simple router that does the following: 
class Router(object):
	def allow_migrate(self, db, model):
		if db == 'default':
			return True
		return False
Current Behaviour
We run our functional tests and the migrate command is called against each connection when the test databases are created (see django/test/runner.py, setup_databases, line 300-ish, which calls django/db/backends/creation.py, create_test_db, line 377-ish)
When this migrate runs, it tries to apply our migrations, which tries to record that a migration has been applied (see django/db/migrations/executor.py, apply_migration, which has several calls to self.recorder.record_applied). 
The first thing that record_applied does is a call to self.ensure_schema() (see django/db/migrations/recorder.py, record_applied, lien 66-ish). 
ensure_schema checks to see if the Migration model is in the tables in the connection. If it does not find the table then it tries to create the table. 
I believe that this is incorrect behaviour when a db_router has been provided. If using the router above, my expectation would be that the table is not created on any connection other than the 'default' connection. Looking at the other methods on the MigrationRecorder, I would expect that there will be similar issues with applied_migrations and record_unapplied.

### GitHub Problem Description ###
Messages framework incorrectly serializes/deserializes extra_tags when it's an empty string
Description
	
When a message is serialised and then deserialised with any of the built in storage backends, then extra_tags=="" is converted to extra_tags==None. This is because MessageEncoder checks for the truthyness of extra_tags rather than checking it is not None.
To replicate this bug
>>> from django.conf import settings
>>> settings.configure() # Just to allow the following import
>>> from django.contrib.messages.storage.base import Message
>>> from django.contrib.messages.storage.cookie import MessageEncoder, MessageDecoder
>>> original_message = Message(10, "Here is a message", extra_tags="")
>>> encoded_message = MessageEncoder().encode(original_message)
>>> decoded_message = MessageDecoder().decode(encoded_message)
>>> original_message.extra_tags == ""
True
>>> decoded_message.extra_tags is None
True
Effect of the bug in application behaviour
This error occurred in the wild with a template tag similar to the following:
{% if x not in message.extra_tags %}
When the message was displayed as part of a redirect, it had been serialised and deserialized which meant that extra_tags was None instead of the empty string. This caused an error.
It's important to note that this bug affects all of the standard API (messages.debug, messages.info etc. all have a default value of extra_tags equal to "").

368|    def rewrite_cols(self, annotation, col_cnt):
369|        # We must make sure the inner query has the referred columns in it.
370|        # If we are aggregating over an annotation, then Django uses Ref()
371|        # instances to note this. However, if we are annotating over a column
372|        # of a related model, then it might be that column isn't part of the
373|        # SELECT clause of the inner query, and we must manually make sure
374|        # the column is selected. An example case is:
375|        #    .aggregate(Sum('author__awards'))
376|        # Resolving this expression results in a join to author, but there
377|        # is no guarantee the awards column of author is in the select clause
378|        # of the query. Thus we must manually add the column to the inner
379|        # query.
380|        orig_exprs = annotation.get_source_expressions()
381|        new_exprs = []
382|        for expr in orig_exprs:
383|            # FIXME: These conditions are fairly arbitrary. Identify a better
384|            # method of having expressions decide which code path they should
385|            # take.
386|            if isinstance(expr, Ref):
387|                # Its already a Ref to subquery (see resolve_ref() for
388|                # details)
389|                new_exprs.append(expr)
390|            elif isinstance(expr, (WhereNode, Lookup)):
391|                # Decompose the subexpressions further. The code here is
392|                # copied from the else clause, but this condition must appear
393|                # before the contains_aggregate/is_summary condition below.
394|                new_expr, col_cnt = self.rewrite_cols(expr, col_cnt)
395|                new_exprs.append(new_expr)
396|            else:
397|                # Reuse aliases of expressions already selected in subquery.
398|                for col_alias, selected_annotation in self.annotation_select.items():
399|                    if selected_annotation is expr:
400|                        new_expr = Ref(col_alias, expr)
401|                        break
402|                else:
403|                    # An expression that is not selected the subquery.
404|                    if isinstance(expr, Col) or (expr.contains_aggregate and not expr.is_summary):
405|                        # Reference column or another aggregate. Select it
406|                        # under a non-conflicting alias.
407|                        col_cnt += 1
408|                        col_alias = '__col%d' % col_cnt
409|                        self.annotations[col_alias] = expr
410|                        self.append_annotation_mask([col_alias])
411|                        new_expr = Ref(col_alias, expr)
412|                    else:
413|                        # Some other expression not referencing database values
414|                        # directly. Its subexpression might contain Cols.
415|                        new_expr, col_cnt = self.rewrite_cols(expr, col_cnt)
416|                new_exprs.append(new_expr)
417|        annotation.set_source_expressions(new_exprs)
418|        return annotation, col_cnt

420|    def get_aggregation(self, using, added_aggregate_names):
421|        """
422|        Return the dictionary with the values of the existing aggregations.
423|        """
424|        if not self.annotation_select:
425|            return {}
426|        existing_annotations = [
427|            annotation for alias, annotation
428|            in self.annotations.items()
429|            if alias not in added_aggregate_names
430|        ]
431|        # Decide if we need to use a subquery.
432|        #
433|        # Existing annotations would cause incorrect results as get_aggregation()
434|        # must produce just one result and thus must not use GROUP BY. But we
435|        # aren't smart enough to remove the existing annotations from the
436|        # query, so those would force us to use GROUP BY.
437|        #
438|        # If the query has limit or distinct, or uses set operations, then
439|        # those operations must be done in a subquery so that the query
440|        # aggregates on the limit and/or distinct results instead of applying
441|        # the distinct and limit after the aggregation.
442|        if (isinstance(self.group_by, tuple) or self.is_sliced or existing_annotations or
443|                self.distinct or self.combinator):
444|            from django.db.models.sql.subqueries import AggregateQuery
445|            inner_query = self.clone()
446|            inner_query.subquery = True
447|            outer_query = AggregateQuery(self.model, inner_query)
448|            inner_query.select_for_update = False
449|            inner_query.select_related = False
450|            inner_query.set_annotation_mask(self.annotation_select)
451|            # Queries with distinct_fields need ordering and when a limit is
452|            # applied we must take the slice from the ordered query. Otherwise
453|            # no need for ordering.
454|            inner_query.clear_ordering(force=False)
455|            if not inner_query.distinct:
456|                # If the inner query uses default select and it has some
457|                # aggregate annotations, then we must make sure the inner
458|                # query is grouped by the main model's primary key. However,
459|                # clearing the select clause can alter results if distinct is
460|                # used.
461|                has_existing_aggregate_annotations = any(
462|                    annotation for annotation in existing_annotations
463|                    if getattr(annotation, 'contains_aggregate', True)
464|                )
465|                if inner_query.default_cols and has_existing_aggregate_annotations:
466|                    inner_query.group_by = (self.model._meta.pk.get_col(inner_query.get_initial_alias()),)
467|                inner_query.default_cols = False
468|
469|            relabels = {t: 'subquery' for t in inner_query.alias_map}
470|            relabels[None] = 'subquery'
471|            # Remove any aggregates marked for reduction from the subquery
472|            # and move them to the outer AggregateQuery.
473|            col_cnt = 0
474|            for alias, expression in list(inner_query.annotation_select.items()):
475|                annotation_select_mask = inner_query.annotation_select_mask
476|                if expression.is_summary:
477|                    expression, col_cnt = inner_query.rewrite_cols(expression, col_cnt)
478|                    outer_query.annotations[alias] = expression.relabeled_clone(relabels)
479|                    del inner_query.annotations[alias]
480|                    annotation_select_mask.remove(alias)
481|                # Make sure the annotation_select wont use cached results.
482|                inner_query.set_annotation_mask(inner_query.annotation_select_mask)
483|            if inner_query.select == () and not inner_query.default_cols and not inner_query.annotation_select_mask:
484|                # In case of Model.objects[0:3].count(), there would be no
485|                # field selected in the inner query, yet we must use a subquery.
486|                # So, make sure at least one field is selected.
487|                inner_query.select = (self.model._meta.pk.get_col(inner_query.get_initial_alias()),)
488|        else:
489|            outer_query = self
490|            self.select = ()
491|            self.default_cols = False
492|            self.extra = {}
493|
494|        empty_set_result = [
495|            expression.empty_result_set_value
496|            for expression in outer_query.annotation_select.values()
497|        ]
498|        elide_empty = not any(result is NotImplemented for result in empty_set_result)
499|        outer_query.clear_ordering(force=True)
500|        outer_query.clear_limits()
501|        outer_query.select_for_update = False
502|        outer_query.select_related = False
503|        compiler = outer_query.get_compiler(using, elide_empty=elide_empty)
504|        result = compiler.execute_sql(SINGLE)
505|        if result is None:
506|            result = empty_set_result
507|
508|        converters = compiler.get_converters(outer_query.annotation_select.values())
509|        result = next(compiler.apply_converters((result,), converters))
510|
511|        return dict(zip(outer_query.annotation_select, result))

557|    def combine(self, rhs, connector):
558|        """
559|        Merge the 'rhs' query into the current one (with any 'rhs' effects
560|        being applied *after* (that is, "to the right of") anything in the
561|        current query. 'rhs' is not modified during a call to this function.
562|
563|        The 'connector' parameter describes how to connect filters from the
564|        'rhs' query.
565|        """
566|        if self.model != rhs.model:
567|            raise TypeError('Cannot combine queries on two different base models.')
568|        if self.is_sliced:
569|            raise TypeError('Cannot combine queries once a slice has been taken.')
570|        if self.distinct != rhs.distinct:
571|            raise TypeError('Cannot combine a unique query with a non-unique query.')
572|        if self.distinct_fields != rhs.distinct_fields:
573|            raise TypeError('Cannot combine queries with different distinct fields.')
574|
575|        # If lhs and rhs shares the same alias prefix, it is possible to have
576|        # conflicting alias changes like T4 -> T5, T5 -> T6, which might end up
577|        # as T4 -> T6 while combining two querysets. To prevent this, change an
578|        # alias prefix of the rhs and update current aliases accordingly,
579|        # except if the alias is the base table since it must be present in the
580|        # query on both sides.
581|        initial_alias = self.get_initial_alias()
582|        rhs.bump_prefix(self, exclude={initial_alias})
583|
584|        # Work out how to relabel the rhs aliases, if necessary.
585|        change_map = {}
586|        conjunction = (connector == AND)
587|
588|        # Determine which existing joins can be reused. When combining the
589|        # query with AND we must recreate all joins for m2m filters. When
590|        # combining with OR we can reuse joins. The reason is that in AND
591|        # case a single row can't fulfill a condition like:
592|        #     revrel__col=1 & revrel__col=2
593|        # But, there might be two different related rows matching this
594|        # condition. In OR case a single True is enough, so single row is
595|        # enough, too.
596|        #
597|        # Note that we will be creating duplicate joins for non-m2m joins in
598|        # the AND case. The results will be correct but this creates too many
599|        # joins. This is something that could be fixed later on.
600|        reuse = set() if conjunction else set(self.alias_map)
601|        joinpromoter = JoinPromoter(connector, 2, False)
602|        joinpromoter.add_votes(
603|            j for j in self.alias_map if self.alias_map[j].join_type == INNER)
604|        rhs_votes = set()
605|        # Now, add the joins from rhs query into the new query (skipping base
606|        # table).
607|        rhs_tables = list(rhs.alias_map)[1:]
608|        for alias in rhs_tables:
609|            join = rhs.alias_map[alias]
610|            # If the left side of the join was already relabeled, use the
611|            # updated alias.
612|            join = join.relabeled_clone(change_map)
613|            new_alias = self.join(join, reuse=reuse)
614|            if join.join_type == INNER:
615|                rhs_votes.add(new_alias)
616|            # We can't reuse the same join again in the query. If we have two
617|            # distinct joins for the same connection in rhs query, then the
618|            # combined query must have two joins, too.
619|            reuse.discard(new_alias)
620|            if alias != new_alias:
621|                change_map[alias] = new_alias
622|            if not rhs.alias_refcount[alias]:
623|                # The alias was unused in the rhs query. Unref it so that it
624|                # will be unused in the new query, too. We have to add and
625|                # unref the alias so that join promotion has information of
626|                # the join type for the unused alias.
627|                self.unref_alias(new_alias)
628|        joinpromoter.add_votes(rhs_votes)
629|        joinpromoter.update_join_types(self)
630|
631|        # Combine subqueries aliases to ensure aliases relabelling properly
632|        # handle subqueries when combining where and select clauses.
633|        self.subq_aliases |= rhs.subq_aliases
634|
635|        # Now relabel a copy of the rhs where-clause and add it to the current
636|        # one.
637|        w = rhs.where.clone()
638|        w.relabel_aliases(change_map)
639|        self.where.add(w, connector)
640|
641|        # Selection columns and extra extensions are those provided by 'rhs'.
642|        if rhs.select:
643|            self.set_select([col.relabeled_clone(change_map) for col in rhs.select])
644|        else:
645|            self.select = ()
646|
647|        if connector == OR:
648|            # It would be nice to be able to handle this, but the queries don't
649|            # really make sense (or return consistent value sets). Not worth
650|            # the extra complexity when you can write a real query instead.
651|            if self.extra and rhs.extra:
652|                raise ValueError("When merging querysets using 'or', you cannot have extra(select=...) on both sides.")
653|        self.extra.update(rhs.extra)
654|        extra_select_mask = set()
655|        if self.extra_select_mask is not None:
656|            extra_select_mask.update(self.extra_select_mask)
657|        if rhs.extra_select_mask is not None:
658|            extra_select_mask.update(rhs.extra_select_mask)
659|        if extra_select_mask:
660|            self.set_extra_mask(extra_select_mask)
661|        self.extra_tables += rhs.extra_tables
662|
663|        # Ordering uses the 'rhs' ordering, unless it has none, in which case
664|        # the current ordering is used.
665|        self.order_by = rhs.order_by or self.order_by
666|        self.extra_order_by = rhs.extra_order_by or self.extra_order_by
667|
668|    def deferred_to_data(self, target, callback):
669|        """
670|        Convert the self.deferred_loading data structure to an alternate data
671|        structure, describing the field that *will* be loaded. This is used to
672|        compute the columns to select from the database and also by the
673|        QuerySet class to work out which fields are being initialized on each
674|        model. Models that have all their fields included aren't mentioned in
675|        the result, only those that have field restrictions in place.
676|
677|        The "target" parameter is the instance that is populated (in place).
678|        The "callback" is a function that is called whenever a (model, field)
679|        pair need to be added to "target". It accepts three parameters:
680|        "target", and the model and list of fields being added for that model.
681|        """
682|        field_names, defer = self.deferred_loading
683|        if not field_names:
684|            return
685|        orig_opts = self.get_meta()
686|        seen = {}
687|        must_include = {orig_opts.concrete_model: {orig_opts.pk}}
688|        for field_name in field_names:
689|            parts = field_name.split(LOOKUP_SEP)
690|            cur_model = self.model._meta.concrete_model
691|            opts = orig_opts
692|            for name in parts[:-1]:
693|                old_model = cur_model
694|                if name in self._filtered_relations:
695|                    name = self._filtered_relations[name].relation_name
696|                source = opts.get_field(name)
697|                if is_reverse_o2o(source):
698|                    cur_model = source.related_model
699|                else:
700|                    cur_model = source.remote_field.model
701|                opts = cur_model._meta
702|                # Even if we're "just passing through" this model, we must add
703|                # both the current model's pk and the related reference field
704|                # (if it's not a reverse relation) to the things we select.
705|                if not is_reverse_o2o(source):
706|                    must_include[old_model].add(source)
707|                add_to_dict(must_include, cur_model, opts.pk)
708|            field = opts.get_field(parts[-1])
709|            is_reverse_object = field.auto_created and not field.concrete
710|            model = field.related_model if is_reverse_object else field.model
711|            model = model._meta.concrete_model
712|            if model == opts.model:
713|                model = cur_model
714|            if not is_reverse_o2o(field):
715|                add_to_dict(seen, model, field)
716|
717|        if defer:
718|            # We need to load all fields for each model, except those that
719|            # appear in "seen" (for all models that appear in "seen"). The only
720|            # slight complexity here is handling fields that exist on parent
721|            # models.
722|            workset = {}
723|            for model, values in seen.items():
724|                for field in model._meta.local_fields:
725|                    if field not in values:
726|                        m = field.model._meta.concrete_model
727|                        add_to_dict(workset, m, field)
728|            for model, values in must_include.items():
729|                # If we haven't included a model in workset, we don't add the
730|                # corresponding must_include fields for that model, since an
731|                # empty set means "include all fields". That's why there's no
732|                # "else" branch here.
733|                if model in workset:
734|                    workset[model].update(values)
735|            for model, values in workset.items():
736|                callback(target, model, values)
737|        else:
738|            for model, values in must_include.items():
739|                if model in seen:
740|                    seen[model].update(values)
741|                else:
742|                    # As we've passed through this model, but not explicitly
743|                    # included any fields, we have to make sure it's mentioned
744|                    # so that only the "must include" fields are pulled in.
745|                    seen[model] = values
746|            # Now ensure that every model in the inheritance chain is mentioned
747|            # in the parent list. Again, it must be mentioned to ensure that
748|            # only "must include" fields are pulled in.
749|            for model in orig_opts.get_parent_list():
750|                seen.setdefault(model, set())
751|            for model, values in seen.items():
752|                callback(target, model, values)

754|    def table_alias(self, table_name, create=False, filtered_relation=None):
755|        """
756|        Return a table alias for the given table_name and whether this is a
757|        new alias or not.
758|
759|        If 'create' is true, a new alias is always created. Otherwise, the
760|        most recently created alias for the table (if one exists) is reused.
761|        """
762|        alias_list = self.table_map.get(table_name)
763|        if not create and alias_list:
764|            alias = alias_list[0]
765|            self.alias_refcount[alias] += 1
766|            return alias, False
767|
768|        # Create a new alias for this table.
769|        if alias_list:
770|            alias = '%s%d' % (self.alias_prefix, len(self.alias_map) + 1)
771|            alias_list.append(alias)
772|        else:
773|            # The first occurrence of a table uses the table name directly.
774|            alias = filtered_relation.alias if filtered_relation is not None else table_name
775|            self.table_map[table_name] = [alias]
776|        self.alias_refcount[alias] = 1
777|        return alias, True

787|    def promote_joins(self, aliases):
788|        """
789|        Promote recursively the join type of given aliases and its children to
790|        an outer join. If 'unconditional' is False, only promote the join if
791|        it is nullable or the parent join is an outer join.
792|
793|        The children promotion is done to avoid join chains that contain a LOUTER
794|        b INNER c. So, if we have currently a INNER b INNER c and a->b is promoted,
795|        then we must also promote b->c automatically, or otherwise the promotion
796|        of a->b doesn't actually change anything in the query results.
797|        """
798|        aliases = list(aliases)
799|        while aliases:
800|            alias = aliases.pop(0)
801|            if self.alias_map[alias].join_type is None:
802|                # This is the base table (first FROM entry) - this table
803|                # isn't really joined at all in the query, so we should not
804|                # alter its join type.
805|                continue
806|            # Only the first alias (skipped above) should have None join_type
807|            assert self.alias_map[alias].join_type is not None
808|            parent_alias = self.alias_map[alias].parent_alias
809|            parent_louter = parent_alias and self.alias_map[parent_alias].join_type == LOUTER
810|            already_louter = self.alias_map[alias].join_type == LOUTER
811|            if ((self.alias_map[alias].nullable or parent_louter) and
812|                    not already_louter):
813|                self.alias_map[alias] = self.alias_map[alias].promote()
814|                # Join type of 'alias' changed, so re-examine all aliases that
815|                # refer to this one.
816|                aliases.extend(
817|                    join for join in self.alias_map
818|                    if self.alias_map[join].parent_alias == alias and join not in aliases
819|                )
820|
821|    def demote_joins(self, aliases):
822|        """
823|        Change join type from LOUTER to INNER for all joins in aliases.
824|
825|        Similarly to promote_joins(), this method must ensure no join chains
826|        containing first an outer, then an inner join are generated. If we
827|        are demoting b->c join in chain a LOUTER b LOUTER c then we must
828|        demote a->b automatically, or otherwise the demotion of b->c doesn't
829|        actually change anything in the query results. .
830|        """
831|        aliases = list(aliases)
832|        while aliases:
833|            alias = aliases.pop(0)
834|            if self.alias_map[alias].join_type == LOUTER:
835|                self.alias_map[alias] = self.alias_map[alias].demote()
836|                parent_alias = self.alias_map[alias].parent_alias
837|                if self.alias_map[parent_alias].join_type == INNER:
838|                    aliases.append(parent_alias)

840|    def reset_refcounts(self, to_counts):
841|        """
842|        Reset reference counts for aliases so that they match the value passed
843|        in `to_counts`.
844|        """
845|        for alias, cur_refcount in self.alias_refcount.copy().items():

891|    def bump_prefix(self, other_query, exclude=None):
892|        """
893|        Change the alias prefix to the next letter in the alphabet in a way
894|        that the other query's aliases and this query's aliases will not
895|        conflict. Even tables that previously had no alias will get an alias
896|        after this call. To prevent changing aliases use the exclude parameter.
897|        """
898|        def prefix_gen():
899|            """
900|            Generate a sequence of characters in alphabetical order:
901|                -> 'A', 'B', 'C', ...
902|
903|            When the alphabet is finished, the sequence will continue with the
904|            Cartesian product:
905|                -> 'AA', 'AB', 'AC', ...
906|            """
907|            alphabet = ascii_uppercase
908|            prefix = chr(ord(self.alias_prefix) + 1)
909|            yield prefix
910|            for n in count(1):
911|                seq = alphabet[alphabet.index(prefix):] if prefix else alphabet
912|                for s in product(seq, repeat=n):
913|                    yield ''.join(s)
914|                prefix = None
915|
916|        if self.alias_prefix != other_query.alias_prefix:
917|            # No clashes between self and outer query should be possible.
918|            return
919|
920|        # Explicitly avoid infinite loop. The constant divider is based on how
921|        # much depth recursive subquery references add to the stack. This value
922|        # might need to be adjusted when adding or removing function calls from
923|        # the code path in charge of performing these operations.
924|        local_recursion_limit = sys.getrecursionlimit() // 16
925|        for pos, prefix in enumerate(prefix_gen()):
926|            if prefix not in self.subq_aliases:
927|                self.alias_prefix = prefix
928|                break
929|            if pos > local_recursion_limit:
930|                raise RecursionError(
931|                    'Maximum recursion depth exceeded: too many subqueries.'
932|                )
933|        self.subq_aliases = self.subq_aliases.union([self.alias_prefix])
934|        other_query.subq_aliases = other_query.subq_aliases.union(self.subq_aliases)
935|        if exclude is None:
936|            exclude = {}
937|        self.change_aliases({
938|            alias: '%s%d' % (self.alias_prefix, pos)
939|            for pos, alias in enumerate(self.alias_map)
940|            if alias not in exclude
941|        })

963|    def join(self, join, reuse=None):
964|        """
965|        Return an alias for the 'join', either reusing an existing alias for
966|        that join or creating a new one. 'join' is either a base_table_class or
967|        join_class.

969|        The 'reuse' parameter can be either None which means all joins are
970|        reusable, or it can be a set containing the aliases that can be reused.
971|
972|        A join is always created as LOUTER if the lhs alias is LOUTER to make
973|        sure chains like t1 LOUTER t2 INNER t3 aren't generated. All new
974|        joins are created as LOUTER if the join is nullable.
975|        """
976|        reuse_aliases = [
977|            a for a, j in self.alias_map.items()
978|            if (reuse is None or a in reuse) and j.equals(join)
979|        ]
980|        if reuse_aliases:
981|            if join.table_alias in reuse_aliases:
982|                reuse_alias = join.table_alias
983|            else:
984|                # Reuse the most recent alias of the joined table
985|                # (a many-to-many relation may be joined multiple times).
986|                reuse_alias = reuse_aliases[-1]

989|
990|        # No reuse is possible, so we need a new alias.
991|        alias, _ = self.table_alias(join.table_name, create=True, filtered_relation=join.filtered_relation)

993|            if self.alias_map[join.parent_alias].join_type == LOUTER or join.nullable:
994|                join_type = LOUTER
995|            else:
996|                join_type = INNER
997|            join.join_type = join_type

1000|        return alias

1002|    def join_parent_model(self, opts, model, alias, seen):
1003|        """
1004|        Make sure the given 'model' is joined in the query. If 'model' isn't
1005|        a parent of 'opts' or if it is None this method is a no-op.
1006|
1007|        The 'alias' is the root alias for starting the join, 'seen' is a dict
1008|        of model -> alias of existing joins. It must also contain a mapping
1009|        of None -> some alias. This will be returned in the no-op case.
1010|        """
1011|        if model in seen:
1012|            return seen[model]

1014|        if not chain:
1015|            return alias
1016|        curr_opts = opts
1017|        for int_model in chain:
1018|            if int_model in seen:
1019|                curr_opts = int_model._meta
1020|                alias = seen[int_model]
1021|                continue
1022|            # Proxy model have elements in base chain
1023|            # with no parents, assign the new options
1024|            # object and skip to the next base in that
1025|            # case
1026|            if not curr_opts.parents[int_model]:
1027|                curr_opts = int_model._meta
1028|                continue
