184|def cut_lines(pre: int, post: int = 0, what: str = None) -> Callable:
185|    """Return a listener that removes the first *pre* and last *post*
186|    lines of every docstring.  If *what* is a sequence of strings,
187|    only docstrings of a type in *what* will be processed.
188|
189|    Use like this (e.g. in the ``setup()`` function of :file:`conf.py`)::
190|
191|       from sphinx.ext.autodoc import cut_lines
192|       app.connect('autodoc-process-docstring', cut_lines(4, what=['module']))

195|    """
196|    def process(app: Sphinx, what_: str, name: str, obj: Any, options: Any, lines: List[str]
197|                ) -> None:
198|        if what and what_ not in what:
199|            return
200|        del lines[:pre]
201|        if post:
202|            # remove one trailing blank line.
203|            if lines and not lines[-1]:
204|                lines.pop(-1)
205|            del lines[-post:]
206|        # make sure there is a blank line at the end
207|        if lines and lines[-1]:

212|def between(marker: str, what: Sequence[str] = None, keepempty: bool = False,
213|            exclude: bool = False) -> Callable:
214|    """Return a listener that either keeps, or if *exclude* is True excludes,
215|    lines between lines that match the *marker* regular expression.  If no line
216|    matches, the resulting docstring would be empty, so no change will be made
217|    unless *keepempty* is true.
218|
219|    If *what* is a sequence of strings, only docstrings of a type in *what* will
220|    be processed.
221|    """
222|    marker_re = re.compile(marker)
223|
224|    def process(app: Sphinx, what_: str, name: str, obj: Any, options: Any, lines: List[str]
225|                ) -> None:
226|        if what and what_ not in what:
227|            return
228|        deleted = 0
229|        delete = not exclude
230|        orig_lines = lines[:]
231|        for i, line in enumerate(orig_lines):
232|            if delete:
233|                lines.pop(i - deleted)
234|                deleted += 1
235|            if marker_re.match(line):
236|                delete = not delete
237|                if delete:
238|                    lines.pop(i - deleted)
239|                    deleted += 1
240|        if not lines and not keepempty:
241|            lines[:] = orig_lines
242|        # make sure there is a blank line at the end
243|        if lines and lines[-1]:
244|            lines.append('')
245|    return process

317|            # The code uses the following heuristic:

319|            # b) place them after an (empty) Footnotes rubric
320|            # c) create an empty Footnotes rubric at the end of the document
321|            fns = tree.traverse(nodes.footnote)
322|            if fns:

325|            for node in tree.traverse(nodes.rubric):

328|            doc = tree.traverse(nodes.document)[0]

330|            rub.append(nodes.Text(FOOTNOTES_RUBRIC_NAME))

332|            return doc, doc.index(rub) + 1
333|
334|        if show_urls == 'no':

336|        if show_urls == 'footnote':
337|            doc = tree.traverse(nodes.document)[0]
338|            fn_spot, fn_idx = footnote_spot(tree)

758|                    keep = False

812|    def document_members(self, all_members: bool = False) -> None:
813|        """Generate reST for member documentation.

830|        for (mname, member, isattr) in self.filter_members(members, want_all):

832|                       if cls.can_document_member(member, mname, isattr, self)]
833|            if not classes:

835|                continue
836|            # prefer the documenter with the highest priority
837|            classes.sort(key=lambda cls: cls.priority)
838|            # give explicitly separated module name, so that members
839|            # of inner classes can be documented

841|                '.'.join(self.objpath + [mname])

845|        member_order = self.options.member_order or self.config.autodoc_member_order

848|        for documenter, isattr in memberdocumenters:

850|                all_members=True, real_modname=self.real_modname,
851|                check_module=members_check_module and not isattr)

857|    def sort_members(self, documenters: List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]],
858|                     order: str) -> List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]]:
859|        """Sort the given member list."""
860|        if order == 'groupwise':
861|            # sort by group; alphabetically within groups
862|            documenters.sort(key=lambda e: (e[0].member_order, e[0].name))
863|        elif order == 'bysource':
864|            if self.analyzer:
865|                # sort by source order, by virtue of the module analyzer
866|                tagorder = self.analyzer.tagorder
867|
868|                def keyfunc(entry: Tuple[Documenter, bool]) -> int:
869|                    fullname = entry[0].name.split('::')[1]
870|                    return tagorder.get(fullname, len(tagorder))
871|                documenters.sort(key=keyfunc)
872|            else:
873|                # Assume that member discovery order matches source order.
874|                # This is a reasonable assumption in Python 3.6 and up, where
875|                # module.__dict__ is insertion-ordered.
876|                pass
877|        else:  # alphabetical
878|            documenters.sort(key=lambda e: e[0].name)
879|
880|        return documenters

882|    def generate(self, more_content: Optional[StringList] = None, real_modname: str = None,
883|                 check_module: bool = False, all_members: bool = False) -> None:
884|        """Generate reST for the object given by *self.name*, and possibly for
885|        its members.
886|
887|        If *more_content* is given, include that content. If *real_modname* is
888|        given, use that module name to find attribute docs. If *check_module* is
889|        True, only generate if the object is defined in the module name it is
890|        imported from. If *all_members* is True, document all members.
891|        """
892|        if not self.parse_name():
893|            # need a module to import
894|            logger.warning(
895|                __('don\'t know which module to import for autodocumenting '
896|                   '%r (try placing a "module" or "currentmodule" directive '
897|                   'in the document, or giving an explicit module name)') %
898|                self.name, type='autodoc')
899|            return
900|
901|        # now, import the module and get object to document
902|        if not self.import_object():
903|            return
904|
905|        # If there is no real module defined, figure out which to use.
906|        # The real module is used in the module analyzer to look up the module
907|        # where the attribute documentation would actually be found in.
908|        # This is used for situations where you have a module that collects the
909|        # functions and classes of internal submodules.
910|        guess_modname = self.get_real_modname()
911|        self.real_modname = real_modname or guess_modname
912|

914|        try:
915|            self.analyzer = ModuleAnalyzer.for_module(self.real_modname)
916|            # parse right now, to get PycodeErrors on parsing (results will
917|            # be cached anyway)
918|            self.analyzer.find_attr_docs()
919|        except PycodeError as exc:
920|            logger.debug('[autodoc] module analyzer failed: %s', exc)
921|            # no source file -- e.g. for builtin and C modules
922|            self.analyzer = None

924|            if hasattr(self.module, '__file__') and self.module.__file__:
925|                self.directive.filename_set.add(self.module.__file__)
926|        else:
927|            self.directive.filename_set.add(self.analyzer.srcname)
928|
929|        if self.real_modname != guess_modname:
930|            # Add module to dependency list if target object is defined in other module.
931|            try:
932|                analyzer = ModuleAnalyzer.for_module(guess_modname)
933|                self.directive.filename_set.add(analyzer.srcname)
934|            except PycodeError:
935|                pass
936|
937|        # check __module__ of object (for members not given explicitly)
938|        if check_module:
939|            if not self.check_module():
940|                return
941|
942|        sourcename = self.get_sourcename()
943|
944|        # make sure that the result starts with an empty line.  This is
945|        # necessary for some situations where another directive preprocesses
946|        # reST and no starting newline is present
947|        self.add_line('', sourcename)
948|
949|        # format the object's signature, if any
950|        try:
951|            sig = self.format_signature()
952|        except Exception as exc:
953|            logger.warning(__('error while formatting signature for %s: %s'),
954|                           self.fullname, exc, type='autodoc')
955|            return
956|
957|        # generate the directive header and options, if applicable
958|        self.add_directive_header(sig)
959|        self.add_line('', sourcename)
960|

962|        self.indent += self.content_indent
963|
964|        # add all content (from docstrings, attribute docs etc.)
965|        self.add_content(more_content)
966|
967|        # document members, if possible
968|        self.document_members(all_members)

matematica code printer does not handle floats and derivatives correctly
In its current state the mathematica code printer does not handle Derivative(func(vars), deriver) 
e.g. Derivative(f(t), t) yields Derivative(f(t), t) instead of D[f[t],t]

Also floats with exponents are not handled correctly e.g. 1.0e-4 is not converted to 1.0*^-4

This has an easy fix by adding the following lines to MCodePrinter:


def _print_Derivative(self, expr):
        return "D[%s]" % (self.stringify(expr.args, ", "))

def _print_Float(self, expr):
        res =str(expr)
        return res.replace('e','*^')

### GitHub Problem Description ###
matematica code printer does not handle floats and derivatives correctly
In its current state the mathematica code printer does not handle Derivative(func(vars), deriver) 
e.g. Derivative(f(t), t) yields Derivative(f(t), t) instead of D[f[t],t]

Also floats with exponents are not handled correctly e.g. 1.0e-4 is not converted to 1.0*^-4

This has an easy fix by adding the following lines to MCodePrinter:


def _print_Derivative(self, expr):
        return "D[%s]" % (self.stringify(expr.args, ", "))

def _print_Float(self, expr):
        res =str(expr)
        return res.replace('e','*^')

354|def apart_list_full_decomposition(P, Q, dummygen):
355|    """
356|    Bronstein's full partial fraction decomposition algorithm.
357|
358|    Given a univariate rational function ``f``, performing only GCD
359|    operations over the algebraic closure of the initial ground domain
360|    of definition, compute full partial fraction decomposition with
361|    fractions having linear denominators.
362|
363|    Note that no factorization of the initial denominator of ``f`` is
364|    performed. The final decomposition is formed in terms of a sum of
365|    :class:`RootSum` instances.
366|
367|    References
368|    ==========
369|
370|    1. [Bronstein93]_
371|
372|    """
373|    f, x, U = P/Q, P.gen, []
374|
375|    u = Function('u')(x)
376|    a = Dummy('a')
377|
378|    partial = []
379|
380|    for d, n in Q.sqf_list_include(all=True):
381|        b = d.as_expr()
382|        U += [ u.diff(x, n - 1) ]
383|
384|        h = cancel(f*b**n) / u**n
385|
386|        H, subs = [h], []
387|
388|        for j in range(1, n):
389|            H += [ H[-1].diff(x) / j ]
390|
391|        for j in range(1, n + 1):
392|            subs += [ (U[j - 1], b.diff(x, j) / j) ]
393|
394|        for j in range(0, n):
395|            P, Q = cancel(H[j]).as_numer_denom()
396|
397|            for i in range(0, j + 1):
398|                P = P.subs(*subs[j - i])
399|
400|            Q = Q.subs(*subs[0])
401|
402|            P = Poly(P, x)
403|            Q = Poly(Q, x)
404|
405|            G = P.gcd(d)
406|            D = d.quo(G)
407|
408|            B, g = Q.half_gcdex(D)
409|            b = (P * B.quo(g)).rem(D)
410|
411|            Dw = D.subs(x, next(dummygen))
412|            numer = Lambda(a, b.as_expr().subs(x, a))
413|            denom = Lambda(a, (x - a))
414|            exponent = n-j
415|
416|            partial.append((Dw, numer, denom, exponent))
417|
418|    return partial

99|def main_integrate(expr, facets, hp_params, max_degree=None):
100|    """Function to translate the problem of integrating univariate/bivariate
101|    polynomials over a 2-Polytope to integrating over it's boundary facets.
102|    This is done using Generalized Stokes Theorem and Euler Theorem.
103|
104|    Parameters
105|    ===========
106|    expr : The input polynomial
107|    facets : Facets(Line Segments) of the 2-Polytope
108|    hp_params : Hyperplane Parameters of the facets
109|
110|    Optional Parameters:
111|    max_degree : The maximum degree of any monomial of the input polynomial.
112|
113|    >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
114|    >>> from sympy.integrals.intpoly import main_integrate,\
115|    hyperplane_parameters
116|    >>> from sympy.geometry.polygon import Polygon
117|    >>> from sympy.geometry.point import Point
118|    >>> triangle = Polygon(Point(0, 3), Point(5, 3), Point(1, 1))
119|    >>> facets = triangle.sides
120|    >>> hp_params = hyperplane_parameters(triangle)
121|    >>> main_integrate(x**2 + y**2, facets, hp_params)
122|    325/6
123|    """
124|    dims = (x, y)
125|    dim_length = len(dims)
126|    result = {}
127|    integral_value = S.Zero
128|
129|    if max_degree:
130|        y_degree = max_degree
131|        grad_terms = [[0, 0, 0, 0]] + \
132|            gradient_terms(max_degree)
133|
134|        for facet_count, hp in enumerate(hp_params):
135|            a, b = hp[0], hp[1]
136|            x0 = facets[facet_count].points[0]
137|
138|            for i, monom in enumerate(grad_terms):
139|                #  Every monomial is a tuple :
140|                #  (term, x_degree, y_degree, value over boundary)
141|                m, x_d, y_d, _ = monom
142|                value = result.get(m, None)
143|                if b is S.Zero:
144|                    value_over_boundary = S.Zero
145|                else:
146|                    value_over_boundary = \
147|                        integration_reduction_dynamic(facets, facet_count, a,
148|                                                      b, m, dims, x_d, y_d,
149|                                                      y_degree, x0,
150|                                                      grad_terms, i)
151|                monom[3] = value_over_boundary
152|                degree = x_d + y_d
153|                if value is not None:
154|                    result[m] += value_over_boundary * \
155|                                        (b / norm(a)) / (dim_length + degree)
156|                else:
157|                    result[m] = value_over_boundary * \
158|                                (b / norm(a)) / (dim_length + degree)
159|        return result
160|    else:
161|        polynomials = decompose(expr)
162|        for deg in polynomials:
163|            poly_contribute = S.Zero
164|            facet_count = 0
165|            for hp in hp_params:
166|                value_over_boundary = integration_reduction(facets,
167|                                                            facet_count,
168|                                                            hp[0], hp[1],
169|                                                            polynomials[deg],
170|                                                            dims, deg)
171|                poly_contribute += value_over_boundary * (hp[1] / norm(hp[0]))
172|                facet_count += 1
173|            poly_contribute /= (dim_length + deg)
174|            integral_value += poly_contribute
175|    return integral_value

178|def integration_reduction(facets, index, a, b, expr, dims, degree):
179|    """Helper method for main_integrate. Returns the value of the input
180|    expression evaluated over the polytope facet referenced by a given index.
181|
182|    Parameters
183|    ===========
184|    facets : List of facets of the polytope.
185|    index : Index referencing the facet to integrate the expression over.
186|    a : Hyperplane parameter denoting direction.
187|    b : Hyperplane parameter denoting distance.
188|    expr : The expression to integrate over the facet.
189|    dims : List of symbols denoting axes.
190|    degree : Degree of the homogeneous polynomial.
191|
192|    >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
193|    >>> from sympy.integrals.intpoly import integration_reduction,\
194|    hyperplane_parameters
195|    >>> from sympy.geometry.point import Point
196|    >>> from sympy.geometry.polygon import Polygon
197|    >>> triangle = Polygon(Point(0, 3), Point(5, 3), Point(1, 1))
198|    >>> facets = triangle.sides
199|    >>> a, b = hyperplane_parameters(triangle)[0]
200|    >>> integration_reduction(facets, 0, a, b, 1, (x, y), 0)
201|    5
202|    """
203|    if expr == S.Zero:
204|        return expr
205|
206|    a, b = (S(a[0]), S(a[1])), S(b)
207|
208|    value = S.Zero
209|    x0 = facets[index].points[0]
210|    m = len(facets)
211|    gens = (x, y)
212|
213|    inner_product = diff(expr, gens[0]) * x0[0] + diff(expr, gens[1]) * x0[1]
214|
215|    if inner_product != 0:
216|        value += integration_reduction(facets, index, a, b,
217|                                       inner_product, dims, degree - 1)
218|
219|    value += left_integral(m, index, facets, x0, expr, gens)
220|
221|    return value/(len(dims) + degree - 1)

224|def left_integral(m, index, facets, x0, expr, gens):
225|    """Computes the left integral of Eq 10 in Chin et al.
226|    For the 2D case, the integral is just an evaluation of the polynomial
227|    at the intersection of two facets which is multiplied by the distance
228|    between the first point of facet and that intersection.
229|
230|    Parameters
231|    ===========
232|    m : No. of hyperplanes.
233|    index : Index of facet to find intersections with.
234|    facets : List of facets(Line Segments in 2D case).
235|    x0 : First point on facet referenced by index.
236|    expr : Input polynomial
237|    gens : Generators which generate the polynomial
238|
239|    >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
240|    >>> from sympy.integrals.intpoly import left_integral
241|    >>> from sympy.geometry.point import Point
242|    >>> from sympy.geometry.polygon import Polygon
243|    >>> triangle = Polygon(Point(0, 3), Point(5, 3), Point(1, 1))
244|    >>> facets = triangle.sides
245|    >>> left_integral(3, 0, facets, facets[0].points[0], 1, (x, y))
246|    5
247|    """
248|    value = S.Zero
249|    for j in range(0, m):
250|        intersect = ()
251|        if j == (index - 1) % m or j == (index + 1) % m:
252|            intersect = intersection(facets[index], facets[j])
253|        if intersect:
254|            distance_origin = norm(tuple(map(lambda x, y: x - y,
255|                                             intersect, x0)))
256|            if is_vertex(intersect):
257|                if isinstance(expr, Expr):
258|                    if len(gens) == 3:
259|                        expr_dict = {gens[0]: intersect[0],
260|                                     gens[1]: intersect[1],
261|                                     gens[2]: intersect[2]}
262|                    else:
263|                        expr_dict = {gens[0]: intersect[0],
264|                                     gens[1]: intersect[1]}
265|                    value += distance_origin * expr.subs(expr_dict)
266|                else:
267|                    value += distance_origin * expr
268|    return value

271|def integration_reduction_dynamic(facets, index, a, b, expr,
272|                                  dims, x_degree, y_degree, max_y_degree,
273|                                  x0, monomial_values, monom_index):
274|    """The same integration_reduction function which uses a dynamic
275|    programming approach to compute terms by using the values of the integral
276|    the gradient of previous terms.
277|
278|    Parameters
279|    ===========
280|    facets : Facets of 2-Polytope
281|    index : Index of facet to find intersections with.(Used in left_integral())
282|    a, b : Hyperplane parameters
283|    expr : Input monomial
284|    dims : Tuple denoting axes variables
285|    x_degree : Exponent of 'x' in expr
286|    y_degree : Exponent of 'y' in expr
287|    max_y_degree : Maximum y-exponent of any monomial in monomial_values
288|    x0 : First point on facets[index]
289|    monomial_values : List of monomial values constituting the polynomial
290|    monom_index : Index of monomial whose integration is being found.
291|
292|    >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
293|    >>> from sympy.integrals.intpoly import integration_reduction_dynamic,\
294|    hyperplane_parameters, gradient_terms
295|    >>> from sympy.geometry.point import Point
296|    >>> from sympy.geometry.polygon import Polygon
297|    >>> triangle = Polygon(Point(0, 3), Point(5, 3), Point(1, 1))
298|    >>> facets = triangle.sides
299|    >>> a, b = hyperplane_parameters(triangle)[0]
300|    >>> x0 = facets[0].points[0]
301|    >>> monomial_values = [[0, 0, 0, 0], [1, 0, 0, 5],\
302|                           [y, 0, 1, 15], [x, 1, 0, None]]
303|    >>> integration_reduction_dynamic(facets, 0, a, b, x, (x, y), 1, 0, 1, x0,\
304|                                      monomial_values, 3)
305|    25/2
306|    """
307|    expr = S(expr)
308|    value = S.Zero
309|    degree = x_degree + y_degree
310|    m = len(facets)
311|    gens = (x, y)
312|    if expr == S.Zero:
313|        return expr
314|
315|    if not expr.is_number:
316|        a, b = (S(a[0]), S(a[1])), S(b)
317|
318|        x_index = monom_index - max_y_degree + \
319|            x_degree - 2 if x_degree >= 1 else 0
320|        y_index = monom_index - 1 if y_degree >= 1 else 0
321|
322|        x_value, y_value =\
323|            monomial_values[x_index][3], monomial_values[y_index][3]
324|
325|        value += x_degree * x_value * x0[0] + y_degree * y_value * x0[1]
326|
327|    value += left_integral(m, index, facets, x0, expr, gens)
328|
329|    return value/(len(dims) + degree - 1)

332|def gradient_terms(binomial_power=0):
333|    """Returns a list of all the possible
334|    monomials between 0 and y**binomial_power
335|
336|    Parameters
337|    ===========
338|    binomial_power : Power upto which terms are generated.
339|
340|    Examples
341|    ========
342|    >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
343|    >>> from sympy.integrals.intpoly import gradient_terms
344|    >>> gradient_terms(2)
345|    [[1, 0, 0, None], [y, 0, 1, None], [y**2, 0, 2, None], [x, 1, 0, None],\
346|    [x*y, 1, 1, None], [x**2, 2, 0, None]]
347|
348|    """
349|    terms = []
350|    for x_count in range(0, binomial_power + 1):
351|        for y_count in range(0, binomial_power - x_count + 1):
352|            terms.append([x**x_count*y**y_count,
353|                          x_count, y_count, None])
354|    return terms

357|def hyperplane_parameters(poly):
358|    """A helper function to return the hyperplane parameters
359|    of which the facets of the polygon are a part of.
360|    Currently works for only 2-Polytopes.
361|    Parameters
362|    ==========
363|    poly : The input Polygon
364|
365|    Examples
366|    ========
367|    >>> from sympy.geometry.point import Point
368|    >>> from sympy.geometry.polygon import Polygon
369|    >>> from sympy.integrals.intpoly import hyperplane_parameters
370|    >>> hyperplane_parameters(Polygon(Point(0, 3), Point(5, 3), Point(1, 1)))
371|    [((0, 1), 3), ((1, -2), -1), ((-2, -1), -3)]
372|    """
373|    vertices = list(poly.vertices) + [poly.vertices[0]]  # Close the polygon.
374|    params = [None] * (len(vertices) - 1)
375|    for i in range(len(vertices) - 1):
376|        v1 = vertices[i]
377|        v2 = vertices[i + 1]
378|
379|        a1 = v1[1] - v2[1]
380|        a2 = v2[0] - v1[0]
381|        b = v2[0] * v1[1] - v2[1] * v1[0]
382|
383|        factor = gcd_list([a1, a2, b])
384|
385|        b = S(b)/factor
386|        a = (S(a1)/factor, S(a2)/factor)
387|        params[i] = (a, b)
388|
389|    return params

392|def best_origin(a, b, lineseg, expr):
393|    """Helper method for polytope_integrate.
394|    Returns a point on the lineseg whose vector inner product with the
395|    divergence of `expr` yields an expression with the least maximum
396|    total power.
397|    Parameters
398|    ==========
399|    a : Hyperplane parameter denoting direction.
400|    b : Hyperplane parameter denoting distance.
401|    lineseg : Line segment on which to find the origin.
402|    expr : The expression which determines the best point.
403|    Algorithm(currently works only for 2D use case)
404|    ===============================================
405|    1 > Firstly, check for edge cases. Here that would refer to vertical
406|        or horizontal lines.
407|
408|    2 > If input expression is a polynomial containing more than one generator
409|        then find out the total power of each of the generators.
410|
411|        x**2 + 3 + x*y + x**4*y**5 ---> {x: 7, y: 6}
412|
413|        If expression is a constant value then pick the first boundary point
414|        of the line segment.
415|
416|    3 > First check if a point exists on the line segment where the value of
417|        the highest power generator becomes 0. If not check if the value of
418|        the next highest becomes 0. If none becomes 0 within line segment
419|        constraints then pick the first boundary point of the line segement.
420|        Actually, any point lying on the segment can be picked as best origin
421|        in the last case.
422|    Examples
423|    ========
424|    >>> from sympy.integrals.intpoly import best_origin
425|    >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
426|    >>> from sympy.geometry.line import Segment2D
427|    >>> from sympy.geometry.point import Point
428|    >>> l = Segment2D(Point(0, 3), Point(1, 1))
429|    >>> expr = x**3*y**7
430|    >>> best_origin((2, 1), 3, l, expr)
431|    (0, 3.0)
432|    """
433|    a1, b1 = lineseg.points[0]
434|    def x_axis_cut(ls):
435|        """Returns the point where the input line segment
436|        intersects the x-axis.
437|        Parameters:
438|        ===========
439|        ls : Line segment
440|        """
441|        p, q = ls.points
442|        if p.y == S.Zero:
443|            return tuple(p)
444|        elif q.y == S.Zero:
445|            return tuple(q)
446|        elif p.y/q.y < S.Zero:
447|            return p.y * (p.x - q.x)/(q.y - p.y) + p.x, S.Zero
448|        else:
449|            return ()
450|
451|    def y_axis_cut(ls):
452|        """Returns the point where the input line segment
453|        intersects the y-axis.
454|        Parameters:
455|        ===========
456|        ls : Line segment
457|        """
458|        p, q = ls.points
459|        if p.x == S.Zero:
460|            return tuple(p)
461|        elif q.x == S.Zero:
462|            return tuple(q)
463|        elif p.x/q.x < S.Zero:
464|            return S.Zero, p.x * (p.y - q.y)/(q.x - p.x) + p.y
465|        else:
466|            return ()
467|
468|    gens = (x, y)
469|    power_gens = {}
470|
471|    for i in gens:
472|        power_gens[i] = S.Zero
473|
474|    if len(gens) > 1:
475|        # Special case for vertical and horizontal lines
476|        if len(gens) == 2:
477|            if a[0] == S.Zero:
478|                if y_axis_cut(lineseg):
479|                    return S.Zero, b/a[1]
480|                else:
481|                    return a1, b1
482|            elif a[1] == S.Zero:
483|                if x_axis_cut(lineseg):
484|                    return b/a[0], S.Zero
485|                else:
486|                    return a1, b1
487|
488|        if isinstance(expr, Expr):  # Find the sum total of power of each
489|            if expr.is_Add:         # generator and store in a dictionary.
490|                for monomial in expr.args:
491|                    if monomial.is_Pow:
492|                        if monomial.args[0] in gens:
493|                            power_gens[monomial.args[0]] += monomial.args[1]
494|                    else:
495|                        for univariate in monomial.args:
496|                            term_type = len(univariate.args)
497|                            if term_type == 0 and univariate in gens:
498|                                power_gens[univariate] += 1
499|                            elif term_type == 2 and univariate.args[0] in gens:
500|                                power_gens[univariate.args[0]] +=\
501|                                           univariate.args[1]
502|            elif expr.is_Mul:
503|                for term in expr.args:
504|                    term_type = len(term.args)
505|                    if term_type == 0 and term in gens:
506|                        power_gens[term] += 1
507|                    elif term_type == 2 and term.args[0] in gens:
508|                        power_gens[term.args[0]] += term.args[1]
509|            elif expr.is_Pow:
510|                power_gens[expr.args[0]] = expr.args[1]
511|            elif expr.is_Symbol:
512|                power_gens[expr] += 1
513|        else:  # If `expr` is a constant take first vertex of the line segment.
514|            return a1, b1
515|
516|        #  TODO : This part is quite hacky. Should be made more robust with
517|        #  TODO : respect to symbol names and scalable w.r.t higher dimensions.
518|        power_gens = sorted(power_gens.items(), key=lambda k: str(k[0]))
519|        if power_gens[0][1] >= power_gens[1][1]:
520|            if y_axis_cut(lineseg):
521|                x0 = (S.Zero, b / a[1])
522|            elif x_axis_cut(lineseg):
523|                x0 = (b / a[0], S.Zero)
524|            else:
525|                x0 = (a1, b1)
526|        else:
527|            if x_axis_cut(lineseg):
528|                x0 = (b/a[0], S.Zero)
529|            elif y_axis_cut(lineseg):
530|                x0 = (S.Zero, b/a[1])
531|            else:
532|                x0 = (a1, b1)
533|    else:
534|        x0 = (b/a[0])
535|    return x0

538|def decompose(expr, separate=False):
539|    """Decomposes an input polynomial into homogeneous ones of
540|    smaller or equal degree.
541|    Returns a dictionary with keys as the degree of the smaller
542|    constituting polynomials. Values are the constituting polynomials.
543|    Parameters
544|    ==========
545|    expr : Polynomial(SymPy expression)
546|
547|    Optional Parameters :
548|
549|    separate : If True then simply return a list of the constituent monomials
550|               If not then break up the polynomial into constituent homogeneous
551|               polynomials.
552|    Examples
553|    ========
554|    >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
555|    >>> from sympy.integrals.intpoly import decompose
556|    >>> decompose(x**2 + x*y + x + y + x**3*y**2 + y**5)
557|    {1: x + y, 2: x**2 + x*y, 5: x**3*y**2 + y**5}
558|    >>> decompose(x**2 + x*y + x + y + x**3*y**2 + y**5, True)
559|    [x, y, x**2, y**5, x*y, x**3*y**2]
560|    """
561|    expr = S(expr)
562|    poly_dict = {}
563|
564|    if isinstance(expr, Expr) and not expr.is_number:
565|        if expr.is_Symbol:
566|            poly_dict[1] = expr
567|        elif expr.is_Add:
568|            symbols = expr.atoms(Symbol)
569|            degrees = [(sum(degree_list(monom, *symbols)), monom)
570|                       for monom in expr.args]
571|            if separate:
572|                return [monom[1] for monom in degrees]
573|            else:
574|                for monom in degrees:
575|                    degree, term = monom
576|                    if poly_dict.get(degree):
577|                        poly_dict[degree] += term
578|                    else:
579|                        poly_dict[degree] = term
580|        elif expr.is_Pow:
581|            _, degree = expr.args
582|            poly_dict[degree] = expr
583|        else:  # Now expr can only be of `Mul` type
584|            degree = 0
585|            for term in expr.args:
586|                term_type = len(term.args)
587|                if term_type == 0 and term.is_Symbol:
588|                    degree += 1
589|                elif term_type == 2:
590|                    degree += term.args[1]
591|            poly_dict[degree] = expr
592|    else:
593|        poly_dict[0] = expr
594|
595|    if separate:
596|        return list(poly_dict.values())
597|    return poly_dict

600|def clockwise_sort(poly):
601|    """Returns the same polygon with points sorted in clockwise order.
602|
603|    Note that it's necessary for input points to be sorted in some order
604|    (clockwise or anti-clockwise) for the algorithm to work. As a convention
605|    algorithm has been implemented keeping clockwise orientation in mind.
606|
607|    Parameters
608|    ==========
609|    poly: 2-Polytope
610|
611|    Examples
612|    ========
613|    >>> from sympy.integrals.intpoly import clockwise_sort
614|    >>> from sympy.geometry.point import Point
615|    >>> from sympy.geometry.polygon import Polygon
616|    >>> clockwise_sort(Polygon(Point(0, 0), Point(1, 0), Point(1, 1)))
617|    Triangle(Point2D(1, 1), Point2D(1, 0), Point2D(0, 0))
618|
619|    """
620|    n = len(poly.vertices)
621|    vertices = list(poly.vertices)
622|    center = Point(sum(map(lambda vertex: vertex.x, poly.vertices)) / n,
623|                   sum(map(lambda vertex: vertex.y, poly.vertices)) / n)
624|

1047|    @property
1048|    def cyclic_form(self):
1049|        """
1050|        This is used to convert to the cyclic notation
1051|        from the canonical notation. Singletons are omitted.
1052|
1053|        Examples
1054|        ========
1055|
1056|        >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
1057|        >>> Permutation.print_cyclic = False
1058|        >>> p = Permutation([0, 3, 1, 2])
1059|        >>> p.cyclic_form
1060|        [[1, 3, 2]]
1061|        >>> Permutation([1, 0, 2, 4, 3, 5]).cyclic_form
1062|        [[0, 1], [3, 4]]
1063|

1065|        ========
1066|
1067|        array_form, full_cyclic_form
1068|        """
1069|        if self._cyclic_form is not None:
1070|            return list(self._cyclic_form)
1071|        array_form = self.array_form
1072|        unchecked = [True] * len(array_form)
1073|        cyclic_form = []
1074|        for i in range(len(array_form)):
1075|            if unchecked[i]:
1076|                cycle = []
1077|                cycle.append(i)
1078|                unchecked[i] = False
1079|                j = i
1080|                while unchecked[array_form[j]]:
1081|                    j = array_form[j]
1082|                    cycle.append(j)
1083|                    unchecked[j] = False
1084|                if len(cycle) > 1:
1085|                    cyclic_form.append(cycle)
1086|                    assert cycle == list(minlex(cycle, is_set=True))
1087|        cyclic_form.sort()
1088|        self._cyclic_form = cyclic_form[:]
1089|        return cyclic_form

1103|        rv = self.cyclic_form

1248|    def __mul__(self, other):
1249|        """
1250|        Return the product a*b as a Permutation; the ith value is b(a(i)).

1253|        ========
1254|
1255|        >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import _af_rmul, Permutation
1256|        >>> Permutation.print_cyclic = False
1257|
1258|        >>> a, b = [1, 0, 2], [0, 2, 1]
1259|        >>> a = Permutation(a); b = Permutation(b)
1260|        >>> list(a*b)
1261|        [2, 0, 1]
1262|        >>> [b(a(i)) for i in range(3)]
1263|        [2, 0, 1]

1266|
1267|        >>> al = list(a); bl = list(b)
1268|        >>> _af_rmul(al, bl)
1269|        [1, 2, 0]
1270|        >>> [al[bl[i]] for i in range(3)]

1274|        one will be padded to match the longer one:
1275|
1276|        >>> b*Permutation([1, 0])

1282|        single list to the left of a Permutation:
1283|

1285|        Permutation([1, 0, 2])
1286|        >>> [[0, 1]]*a # exchange first two elements
1287|        Permutation([0, 1, 2])

1291|        multiple cycles it is convenient to use Cycle instead of Permutation:
1292|
1293|        >>> [[1, 2]]*[[2, 3]]*Permutation([]) # doctest: +SKIP
1294|        >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Cycle
1295|        >>> Cycle(1, 2)(2, 3)
1296|        (1 3 2)
1297|
1298|        """

1300|        # __rmul__ makes sure the other is a Permutation

1302|        if not b:
1303|            perm = a
1304|        else:
1305|            b.extend(list(range(len(b), len(a))))

1367|    def __xor__(self, h):
1368|        """Return the conjugate permutation ``~h*self*h` `.
1369|
1370|        If ``a`` and ``b`` are conjugates, ``a = h*b*~h`` and
1371|        ``b = ~h*a*h`` and both have the same cycle structure.
1372|
1373|        Examples
1374|        ========
1375|
1376|        >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
1377|        >>> Permutation.print_cyclic = True
1378|        >>> p = Permutation(1, 2, 9)
1379|        >>> q = Permutation(6, 9, 8)
1380|        >>> p*q != q*p
1381|        True
1382|
1383|        Calculate and check properties of the conjugate:
1384|
1385|        >>> c = p^q
1386|        >>> c == ~q*p*q and p == q*c*~q
1387|        True
1388|
1389|        The expression q^p^r is equivalent to q^(p*r):
1390|
1391|        >>> r = Permutation(9)(4, 6, 8)
1392|        >>> q^p^r == q^(p*r)
1393|        True
1394|
1395|        If the term to the left of the conjugate operator, i, is an integer
1396|        then this is interpreted as selecting the ith element from the
1397|        permutation to the right:
1398|
1399|        >>> all(i^p == p(i) for i in range(p.size))
1400|        True
1401|
1402|        Note that the * operator as higher precedence than the ^ operator:
1403|
1404|        >>> q^r*p^r == q^(r*p)^r == Permutation(9)(1, 6, 4)
1405|        True
1406|
1407|        Notes
1408|        =====
1409|
1410|        In Python the precedence rule is p^q^r = (p^q)^r which differs
1411|        in general from p^(q^r)
1412|
1413|        >>> q^p^r
1414|        (9)(1 4 8)
1415|        >>> q^(p^r)
1416|        (9)(1 8 6)
1417|
1418|        For a given r and p, both of the following are conjugates of p:
1419|        ~r*p*r and r*p*~r. But these are not necessarily the same:
1420|
1421|        >>> ~r*p*r == r*p*~r
1422|        True
1423|
1424|        >>> p = Permutation(1, 2, 9)(5, 6)
1425|        >>> ~r*p*r == r*p*~r
1426|        False
1427|
1428|        The conjugate ~r*p*r was chosen so that ``p^q^r`` would be equivalent
1429|        to ``p^(q*r)`` rather than ``p^(r*q)``. To obtain r*p*~r, pass ~r to
1430|        this method:
1431|
1432|        >>> p^~r == r*p*~r
1433|        True
1434|        """
1435|
1436|        if self.size != h.size:
1437|            raise ValueError("The permutations must be of equal size.")
1438|        a = [None]*self.size
1439|        h = h._array_form
1440|        p = self._array_form
1441|        for i in range(self.size):
1442|            a[h[i]] = h[p[i]]
1443|        return _af_new(a)

1445|    def transpositions(self):
1446|        """
1447|        Return the permutation decomposed into a list of transpositions.
1448|
1449|        It is always possible to express a permutation as the product of
1450|        transpositions, see [1]
1451|
1452|        Examples
1453|        ========
1454|
1455|        >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
1456|        >>> p = Permutation([[1, 2, 3], [0, 4, 5, 6, 7]])
1457|        >>> t = p.transpositions()
1458|        >>> t
1459|        [(0, 7), (0, 6), (0, 5), (0, 4), (1, 3), (1, 2)]
1460|        >>> print(''.join(str(c) for c in t))
1461|        (0, 7)(0, 6)(0, 5)(0, 4)(1, 3)(1, 2)
1462|        >>> Permutation.rmul(*[Permutation([ti], size=p.size) for ti in t]) == p
1463|        True

1465|        References
1466|        ==========
1467|
1468|        1. http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transposition_%28mathematics%29#Properties
1469|
1470|        """
1471|        a = self.cyclic_form
1472|        res = []
1473|        for x in a:
1474|            nx = len(x)
1475|            if nx == 2:
1476|                res.append(tuple(x))
1477|            elif nx > 2:
1478|                first = x[0]
1479|                for y in x[nx - 1:0:-1]:
1480|                    res.append((first, y))
1481|        return res

1595|    def next_lex(self):
1596|        """
1597|        Returns the next permutation in lexicographical order.
1598|        If self is the last permutation in lexicographical order
1599|        it returns None.
1600|        See [4] section 2.4.
1601|
1602|
1603|        Examples
1604|        ========
1605|
1606|        >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
1607|        >>> p = Permutation([2, 3, 1, 0])
1608|        >>> p = Permutation([2, 3, 1, 0]); p.rank()
1609|        17
1610|        >>> p = p.next_lex(); p.rank()
1611|        18
1612|
1613|        See Also
1614|        ========
1615|
1616|        rank, unrank_lex
1617|        """
1618|        perm = self.array_form[:]
1619|        n = len(perm)
1620|        i = n - 2
1621|        while perm[i + 1] < perm[i]:
1622|            i -= 1
1623|        if i == -1:
1624|            return None
1625|        else:
1626|            j = n - 1
1627|            while perm[j] < perm[i]:
1628|                j -= 1
1629|            perm[j], perm[i] = perm[i], perm[j]
1630|            i += 1
1631|            j = n - 1
1632|            while i < j:
1633|                perm[j], perm[i] = perm[i], perm[j]
1634|                i += 1
1635|                j -= 1
1636|        return _af_new(perm)

1638|    @classmethod
1639|    def unrank_nonlex(self, n, r):
1640|        """
1641|        This is a linear time unranking algorithm that does not
1642|        respect lexicographic order [3].
1643|
1644|        Examples
1645|        ========
1646|
1647|        >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
1648|        >>> Permutation.print_cyclic = False
1649|        >>> Permutation.unrank_nonlex(4, 5)
1650|        Permutation([2, 0, 3, 1])
1651|        >>> Permutation.unrank_nonlex(4, -1)
1652|        Permutation([0, 1, 2, 3])
1653|
1654|        See Also
1655|        ========
1656|
1657|        next_nonlex, rank_nonlex
1658|        """
1659|        def _unrank1(n, r, a):
1660|            if n > 0:
1661|                a[n - 1], a[r % n] = a[r % n], a[n - 1]
1662|                _unrank1(n - 1, r//n, a)
1663|
1664|        id_perm = list(range(n))
1665|        n = int(n)
1666|        r = r % ifac(n)
1667|        _unrank1(n, r, id_perm)
1668|        return _af_new(id_perm)

1670|    def rank_nonlex(self, inv_perm=None):
1671|        """

1673|        enforce lexicographic order [3].

1675|
1676|        Examples

1733|    def rank(self):
1734|        """
1735|        Returns the lexicographic rank of the permutation.
1736|
1737|        Examples
1738|        ========
1739|
1740|        >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
1741|        >>> p = Permutation([0, 1, 2, 3])
1742|        >>> p.rank()

1745|        >>> p.rank()
1746|        23

1749|        ========
1750|
1751|        next_lex, unrank_lex, cardinality, length, order, size
1752|        """
1753|        if not self._rank is None:
1754|            return self._rank

1756|        rho = self.array_form[:]
1757|        n = self.size - 1
1758|        size = n + 1
1759|        psize = int(ifac(n))
1760|        for j in range(size - 1):
1761|            rank += rho[j]*psize
1762|            for i in range(j + 1, size):
1763|                if rho[i] > rho[j]:
1764|                    rho[i] -= 1
1765|            psize //= n
1766|            n -= 1

1768|        return rank

2030|    def inversions(self):
2031|        """

2035|

2037|        values and calculates the number of inversions.
2038|        For large length of p, it uses a variation of merge
2039|        sort to calculate the number of inversions.

2042|        ==========
2043|

2053|        >>> Permutation([3, 2, 1, 0]).inversions()
2054|        6

2057|        ========
2058|
2059|        descents, ascents, min, max

2061|        inversions = 0
2062|        a = self.array_form
2063|        n = len(a)
2064|        if n < 130:
2065|            for i in range(n - 1):
2066|                b = a[i]
2067|                for c in a[i + 1:]:
2068|                    if b > c:
2069|                        inversions += 1
2070|        else:
2071|            k = 1
2072|            right = 0
2073|            arr = a[:]
2074|            temp = a[:]
2075|            while k < n:
2076|                i = 0
2077|                while i + k < n:
2078|                    right = i + k * 2 - 1
2079|                    if right >= n:
2080|                        right = n - 1
2081|                    inversions += _merge(arr, temp, i, i + k, right)
2082|                    i = i + k * 2

2086|    def commutator(self, x):
2087|        """Return the commutator of self and x: ``~x*~self*x*self``
2088|
2089|        If f and g are part of a group, G, then the commutator of f and g
2090|        is the group identity iff f and g commute, i.e. fg == gf.
2091|
2092|        Examples
2093|        ========
2094|
2095|        >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
2096|        >>> Permutation.print_cyclic = False
2097|        >>> p = Permutation([0, 2, 3, 1])
2098|        >>> x = Permutation([2, 0, 3, 1])
2099|        >>> c = p.commutator(x); c
2100|        Permutation([2, 1, 3, 0])
2101|        >>> c == ~x*~p*x*p
2102|        True
2103|
2104|        >>> I = Permutation(3)
2105|        >>> p = [I + i for i in range(6)]
2106|        >>> for i in range(len(p)):
2107|        ...     for j in range(len(p)):
2108|        ...         c = p[i].commutator(p[j])
2109|        ...         if p[i]*p[j] == p[j]*p[i]:
2110|        ...             assert c == I
2111|        ...         else:
2112|        ...             assert c != I
2113|        ...
2114|
2115|        References
2116|        ==========
2117|
2118|        http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commutator
2119|        """
2120|
2121|        a = self.array_form
2122|        b = x.array_form
2123|        n = len(a)
2124|        if len(b) != n:
2125|            raise ValueError("The permutations must be of equal size.")
2126|        inva = [None]*n
2127|        for i in range(n):
2128|            inva[a[i]] = i
2129|        invb = [None]*n
2130|        for i in range(n):
2131|            invb[b[i]] = i
2132|        return _af_new([a[b[inva[i]]] for i in invb])

2302|    def inversion_vector(self):
2303|        """Return the inversion vector of the permutation.
2304|
2305|        The inversion vector consists of elements whose value
2306|        indicates the number of elements in the permutation
2307|        that are lesser than it and lie on its right hand side.

2316|        >>> p = Permutation([4, 8, 0, 7, 1, 5, 3, 6, 2])

2319|        >>> p = Permutation([3, 2, 1, 0])
2320|        >>> p.inversion_vector()
2321|        [3, 2, 1]
2322|
2323|        The inversion vector increases lexicographically with the rank
2324|        of the permutation, the -ith element cycling through 0..i.
2325|
2326|        >>> p = Permutation(2)
2327|        >>> while p:
2328|        ...     print('%s %s %s' % (p, p.inversion_vector(), p.rank()))
2329|        ...     p = p.next_lex()
2330|        ...
2331|        Permutation([0, 1, 2]) [0, 0] 0
2332|        Permutation([0, 2, 1]) [0, 1] 1
2333|        Permutation([1, 0, 2]) [1, 0] 2
2334|        Permutation([1, 2, 0]) [1, 1] 3
2335|        Permutation([2, 0, 1]) [2, 0] 4
2336|        Permutation([2, 1, 0]) [2, 1] 5
2337|

2339|        ========
2340|        from_inversion_vector
2341|        """
2342|        self_array_form = self.array_form
2343|        n = len(self_array_form)
2344|        inversion_vector = [0] * (n - 1)
2345|
2346|        for i in range(n - 1):
2347|            val = 0
2348|            for j in range(i + 1, n):
2349|                if self_array_form[j] < self_array_form[i]:
2350|                    val += 1
2351|            inversion_vector[i] = val

2354|    def rank_trotterjohnson(self):
2355|        """
2356|        Returns the Trotter Johnson rank, which we get from the minimal
2357|        change algorithm. See [4] section 2.4.
2358|
2359|        Examples
2360|        ========
2361|
2362|        >>> from sympy.combinatorics.permutations import Permutation
2363|        >>> p = Permutation([0, 1, 2, 3])
2364|        >>> p.rank_trotterjohnson()
2365|        0
2366|        >>> p = Permutation([0, 2, 1, 3])
2367|        >>> p.rank_trotterjohnson()
2368|        7
2369|
2370|        See Also
2371|        ========
2372|
2373|        unrank_trotterjohnson, next_trotterjohnson
2374|        """
2375|        if self.array_form == [] or self.is_Identity:
2376|            return 0
2377|        if self.array_form == [1, 0]:
2378|            return 1
2379|        perm = self.array_form
2380|        n = self.size
2381|        rank = 0
2382|        for j in range(1, n):
2383|            k = 1
2384|            i = 0
2385|            while perm[i] != j:
2386|                if perm[i] < j:
2387|                    k += 1
2388|                i += 1
2389|            j1 = j + 1
2390|            if rank % 2 == 0:
2391|                rank = j1*rank + j1 - k
2392|            else:
2393|                rank = j1*rank + k - 1
2394|        return rank

657|    def _hprint_Function(self, func):
658|        '''
659|        Logic to decide how to render a function to latex
660|          - if it is a recognized latex name, use the appropriate latex command
661|          - if it is a single letter, just use that letter
662|          - if it is a longer name, then put \operatorname{} around it and be
663|            mindful of undercores in the name
664|        '''
665|        func = self._deal_with_super_sub(func)
666|
667|        if func in accepted_latex_functions:
668|            name = r"\%s" % func
669|        elif len(func) == 1 or func.startswith('\\'):
670|            name = func
671|        else:
672|            name = r"\operatorname{%s}" % func
673|        return name

675|    def _print_Function(self, expr, exp=None):
676|        '''
677|        Render functions to LaTeX, handling functions that LaTeX knows about
678|        e.g., sin, cos, ... by using the proper LaTeX command (\sin, \cos, ...).
679|        For single-letter function names, render them as regular LaTeX math
680|        symbols. For multi-letter function names that LaTeX does not know
681|        about, (e.g., Li, sech) use \operatorname{} so that the function name
682|        is rendered in Roman font and LaTeX handles spacing properly.
683|
684|        expr is the expression involving the function
685|        exp is an exponent
686|        '''
687|        func = expr.func.__name__
688|
689|        if hasattr(self, '_print_' + func):
690|            return getattr(self, '_print_' + func)(expr, exp)
691|        else:
692|            args = [ str(self._print(arg)) for arg in expr.args ]
693|            # How inverse trig functions should be displayed, formats are:
694|            # abbreviated: asin, full: arcsin, power: sin^-1
695|            inv_trig_style = self._settings['inv_trig_style']
696|            # If we are dealing with a power-style inverse trig function
697|            inv_trig_power_case = False
698|            # If it is applicable to fold the argument brackets
699|            can_fold_brackets = self._settings['fold_func_brackets'] and \
700|                len(args) == 1 and \
701|                not self._needs_function_brackets(expr.args[0])
702|
703|            inv_trig_table = ["asin", "acos", "atan", "acot"]
704|
705|            # If the function is an inverse trig function, handle the style
706|            if func in inv_trig_table:
707|                if inv_trig_style == "abbreviated":
708|                    func = func
709|                elif inv_trig_style == "full":
710|                    func = "arc" + func[1:]
711|                elif inv_trig_style == "power":
712|                    func = func[1:]
713|                    inv_trig_power_case = True
714|
715|                    # Can never fold brackets if we're raised to a power
716|                    if exp is not None:
717|                        can_fold_brackets = False
718|
719|            if inv_trig_power_case:
720|                if func in accepted_latex_functions:
721|                    name = r"\%s^{-1}" % func
722|                else:
723|                    name = r"\operatorname{%s}^{-1}" % func
724|            elif exp is not None:
725|                name = r'%s^{%s}' % (self._hprint_Function(func), exp)
726|            else:
727|                name = self._hprint_Function(func)
728|
729|            if can_fold_brackets:
730|                if func in accepted_latex_functions:
731|                    # Wrap argument safely to avoid parse-time conflicts
732|                    # with the function name itself
733|                    name += r" {%s}"
734|                else:
735|                    name += r"%s"
736|            else:
737|                name += r"{\left (%s \right )}"
738|
739|            if inv_trig_power_case and exp is not None:
740|                name += r"^{%s}" % exp
741|
742|            return name % ",".join(args)

466|    def _print_Sum(self, expr):
467|        ascii_mode = not self._use_unicode
468|
469|        def asum(hrequired, lower, upper, use_ascii):
470|            def adjust(s, wid=None, how='<^>'):
471|                if not wid or len(s) > wid:
472|                    return s
473|                need = wid - len(s)
474|                if how == '<^>' or how == "<" or how not in list('<^>'):
475|                    return s + ' '*need
476|                half = need//2
477|                lead = ' '*half
478|                if how == ">":
479|                    return " "*need + s
480|                return lead + s + ' '*(need - len(lead))
481|
482|            h = max(hrequired, 2)
483|            d = h//2
484|            w = d + 1
485|            more = hrequired % 2
486|
487|            lines = []
488|            if use_ascii:
489|                lines.append("_"*(w) + ' ')
490|                lines.append("\%s`" % (' '*(w - 1)))
491|                for i in range(1, d):
492|                    lines.append('%s\\%s' % (' '*i, ' '*(w - i)))
493|                if more:
494|                    lines.append('%s)%s' % (' '*(d), ' '*(w - d)))
495|                for i in reversed(range(1, d)):
496|                    lines.append('%s/%s' % (' '*i, ' '*(w - i)))
497|                lines.append("/" + "_"*(w - 1) + ',')
498|                return d, h + more, lines, 0
499|            else:
500|                w = w + more
501|                d = d + more
502|                vsum = vobj('sum', 4)
503|                lines.append("_"*(w))
504|                for i in range(0, d):
505|                    lines.append('%s%s%s' % (' '*i, vsum[2], ' '*(w - i - 1)))
506|                for i in reversed(range(0, d)):
507|                    lines.append('%s%s%s' % (' '*i, vsum[4], ' '*(w - i - 1)))
508|                lines.append(vsum[8]*(w))
509|                return d, h + 2*more, lines, more
510|
511|        f = expr.function
512|
513|        prettyF = self._print(f)
514|
515|        if f.is_Add:  # add parens
516|            prettyF = prettyForm(*prettyF.parens())
517|
518|        H = prettyF.height() + 2
519|
520|        # \sum \sum \sum ...
521|        first = True
522|        max_upper = 0
523|        sign_height = 0
524|
525|        for lim in expr.limits:
526|            if len(lim) == 3:
527|                prettyUpper = self._print(lim[2])
528|                prettyLower = self._print(Equality(lim[0], lim[1]))
529|            elif len(lim) == 2:
530|                prettyUpper = self._print("")
531|                prettyLower = self._print(Equality(lim[0], lim[1]))
532|            elif len(lim) == 1:
533|                prettyUpper = self._print("")
534|                prettyLower = self._print(lim[0])
535|
536|            max_upper = max(max_upper, prettyUpper.height())
537|
538|            # Create sum sign based on the height of the argument
539|            d, h, slines, adjustment = asum(
540|                H, prettyLower.width(), prettyUpper.width(), ascii_mode)
541|            prettySign = stringPict('')
542|            prettySign = prettyForm(*prettySign.stack(*slines))
543|
544|            if first:
545|                sign_height = prettySign.height()
546|
547|            prettySign = prettyForm(*prettySign.above(prettyUpper))
548|            prettySign = prettyForm(*prettySign.below(prettyLower))
549|
550|            if first:
551|                # change F baseline so it centers on the sign
552|                prettyF.baseline -= d - (prettyF.height()//2 -
553|                                         prettyF.baseline) - adjustment
554|                first = False
555|
556|            # put padding to the right
557|            pad = stringPict('')
558|            pad = prettyForm(*pad.stack(*[' ']*h))
559|            prettySign = prettyForm(*prettySign.right(pad))
560|            # put the present prettyF to the right
561|            prettyF = prettyForm(*prettySign.right(prettyF))
562|
563|        prettyF.baseline = max_upper + sign_height//2
564|        prettyF.binding = prettyForm.MUL
565|        return prettyF

611|

618|        for i in range(M.rows):
619|

621|            for j in range(M.cols):
622|                s = Ms[i, j]
623|
624|                # reshape s to maxw

626|                assert s.width() <= maxw[j]

628|                # hcenter it, +0.5 to the right                        2

631|                wdelta = maxw[j] - s.width()
632|                wleft = wdelta // 2

636|                s = prettyForm(*s.left(' '*wleft))
637|
638|                # we don't need vcenter cells -- this is automatically done in

642|                if D_row is None:

645|

1446|    def _print_nth_root(self, base, expt):
1447|        bpretty = self._print(base)
1448|
1449|        # In very simple cases, use a single-char root sign
1450|        if (self._settings['use_unicode_sqrt_char'] and self._use_unicode
1451|            and expt is S.Half and bpretty.height() == 1
1452|            and (bpretty.width() == 1
1453|                 or (base.is_Integer and base.is_nonnegative))):
1454|            return prettyForm(*bpretty.left(u'\N{SQUARE ROOT}'))
1455|
1456|        # Construct root sign, start with the \/ shape
1457|        _zZ = xobj('/', 1)
1458|        rootsign = xobj('\\', 1) + _zZ
1459|        # Make exponent number to put above it
1460|        if isinstance(expt, Rational):
1461|            exp = str(expt.q)
1462|            if exp == '2':
1463|                exp = ''
1464|        else:
1465|            exp = str(expt.args[0])
1466|        exp = exp.ljust(2)
1467|        if len(exp) > 2:
1468|            rootsign = ' '*(len(exp) - 2) + rootsign
1469|        # Stack the exponent
1470|        rootsign = stringPict(exp + '\n' + rootsign)
1471|        rootsign.baseline = 0
1472|        # Diagonal: length is one less than height of base
1473|        linelength = bpretty.height() - 1
1474|        diagonal = stringPict('\n'.join(
1475|            ' '*(linelength - i - 1) + _zZ + ' '*i
1476|            for i in range(linelength)
1477|        ))
1478|        # Put baseline just below lowest line: next to exp
1479|        diagonal.baseline = linelength - 1
1480|        # Make the root symbol
1481|        rootsign = prettyForm(*rootsign.right(diagonal))
1482|        # Det the baseline to match contents to fix the height
1483|        # but if the height of bpretty is one, the rootsign must be one higher
1484|        rootsign.baseline = max(1, bpretty.baseline)
1485|        #build result
1486|        s = prettyForm(hobj('_', 2 + bpretty.width()))
1487|        s = prettyForm(*bpretty.above(s))
1488|        s = prettyForm(*s.left(rootsign))
1489|        return s

307|                if (abs(e) < 1) == True or e == 1:

310|                    s = 1  # floor = 0
311|                elif re(b).is_nonnegative and (abs(e) < 2) == True:
312|                    s = 1  # floor = 0

317|                        S.Half - e*arg(b)/(2*S.Pi)))
318|                    if s.is_real and _n2(sign(s) - s) == 0:

321|                        s = None

328|                        floor(S.Half - im(e*log(b))/2/S.Pi))

332|                        s = sign(s)

334|                        s = None
335|                except PrecisionExhausted:
336|                    s = None

338|        if s is not None:
339|            return s*Pow(b, e*other)

564|    def _eval_subs(self, old, new):
565|        from sympy import exp, log, Symbol
566|        def _check(ct1, ct2, old):
567|            """Return (bool, pow, remainder_pow) where, if bool is True, then the
568|            exponent of Pow `old` will combine with `pow` so the substitution
569|            is valid, otherwise bool will be False.
570|
571|            For noncommutative objects, `pow` will be an integer, and a factor
572|            `Pow(old.base, remainder_pow)` needs to be included. If there is
573|            no such factor, None is returned. For commutative objects,
574|            remainder_pow is always None.
575|
576|            cti are the coefficient and terms of an exponent of self or old
577|            In this _eval_subs routine a change like (b**(2*x)).subs(b**x, y)
578|            will give y**2 since (b**x)**2 == b**(2*x); if that equality does
579|            not hold then the substitution should not occur so `bool` will be
580|            False.
581|
582|            """
583|            coeff1, terms1 = ct1
584|            coeff2, terms2 = ct2
585|            if terms1 == terms2:
586|                if old.is_commutative:
587|                    # Allow fractional powers for commutative objects
588|                    pow = coeff1/coeff2
589|                    try:
590|                        pow = as_int(pow)
591|                        combines = True
592|                    except ValueError:
593|                        combines = Pow._eval_power(
594|                            Pow(*old.as_base_exp(), evaluate=False),
595|                            pow) is not None
596|                    return combines, pow, None
597|                else:
598|                    # With noncommutative symbols, substitute only integer powers
599|                    if not isinstance(terms1, tuple):
600|                        terms1 = (terms1,)
601|                    if not all(term.is_integer for term in terms1):
602|                        return False, None, None
603|
604|                    try:
605|                        # Round pow toward zero
606|                        pow, remainder = divmod(as_int(coeff1), as_int(coeff2))
607|                        if pow < 0 and remainder != 0:
608|                            pow += 1
609|                            remainder -= as_int(coeff2)
610|
611|                        if remainder == 0:
612|                            remainder_pow = None
613|                        else:
614|                            remainder_pow = Mul(remainder, *terms1)
615|
616|                        return True, pow, remainder_pow
617|                    except ValueError:
618|                        # Can't substitute
619|                        pass
620|
621|            return False, None, None
622|
623|        if old == self.base:
624|            return new**self.exp._subs(old, new)
625|
626|        # issue 10829: (4**x - 3*y + 2).subs(2**x, y) -> y**2 - 3*y + 2
627|        if old.func is self.func and self.exp == old.exp:
628|            l = log(self.base, old.base)
629|            if l.is_Number:
630|                return Pow(new, l)
631|
632|        if old.func is self.func and self.base == old.base:
633|            if self.exp.is_Add is False:
634|                ct1 = self.exp.as_independent(Symbol, as_Add=False)
635|                ct2 = old.exp.as_independent(Symbol, as_Add=False)
636|                ok, pow, remainder_pow = _check(ct1, ct2, old)
637|                if ok:
638|                    # issue 5180: (x**(6*y)).subs(x**(3*y),z)->z**2
639|                    result = self.func(new, pow)
640|                    if remainder_pow is not None:
641|                        result = Mul(result, Pow(old.base, remainder_pow))
642|                    return result
643|            else:  # b**(6*x+a).subs(b**(3*x), y) -> y**2 * b**a
644|                # exp(exp(x) + exp(x**2)).subs(exp(exp(x)), w) -> w * exp(exp(x**2))
645|                oarg = old.exp
646|                new_l = []
647|                o_al = []
648|                ct2 = oarg.as_coeff_mul()
649|                for a in self.exp.args:
650|                    newa = a._subs(old, new)
651|                    ct1 = newa.as_coeff_mul()
652|                    ok, pow, remainder_pow = _check(ct1, ct2, old)
653|                    if ok:
654|                        new_l.append(new**pow)
655|                        if remainder_pow is not None:
656|                            o_al.append(remainder_pow)
657|                        continue
658|                    elif not old.is_commutative and not newa.is_integer:
659|                        # If any term in the exponent is non-integer,
660|                        # we do not do any substitutions in the noncommutative case
661|                        return
662|                    o_al.append(newa)
663|                if new_l:
664|                    new_l.append(Pow(self.base, Add(*o_al), evaluate=False))
665|                    return Mul(*new_l)
666|
667|        if old.func is exp and self.exp.is_real and self.base.is_positive:
668|            ct1 = old.args[0].as_independent(Symbol, as_Add=False)
669|            ct2 = (self.exp*log(self.base)).as_independent(
670|                Symbol, as_Add=False)
671|            ok, pow, remainder_pow = _check(ct1, ct2, old)
672|            if ok:
673|                result = self.func(new, pow)  # (2**x).subs(exp(x*log(2)), z) -> z
674|                if remainder_pow is not None:
675|                    result = Mul(result, Pow(old.base, remainder_pow))
676|                return result

678|    def as_base_exp(self):

680|
681|        If base is 1/Integer, then return Integer, -exp. If this extra
682|        processing is not needed, the base and exp properties will
683|        give the raw arguments
684|
685|        Examples
686|        ========
687|
688|        >>> from sympy import Pow, S
689|        >>> p = Pow(S.Half, 2, evaluate=False)
690|        >>> p.as_base_exp()
691|        (2, -2)
692|        >>> p.args
693|        (1/2, 2)
694|
695|        """
696|
697|        b, e = self.args
698|        if b.is_Rational and b.p == 1 and b.q != 1:
699|            return Integer(b.q), -e
700|        return b, e

740|    def _eval_expand_power_exp(self, **hints):
741|        """a**(n+m) -> a**n*a**m"""
742|        b = self.base
743|        e = self.exp
744|        if e.is_Add and e.is_commutative:
745|            expr = []
746|            for x in e.args:
747|                expr.append(self.func(self.base, x))

751|    def _eval_expand_power_base(self, **hints):
752|        """(a*b)**n -> a**n * b**n"""
753|        force = hints.get('force', False)
754|
755|        b = self.base
756|        e = self.exp
757|        if not b.is_Mul:
758|            return self
759|
760|        cargs, nc = b.args_cnc(split_1=False)
761|
762|        # expand each term - this is top-level-only
763|        # expansion but we have to watch out for things
764|        # that don't have an _eval_expand method
765|        if nc:
766|            nc = [i._eval_expand_power_base(**hints)
767|                if hasattr(i, '_eval_expand_power_base') else i
768|                for i in nc]
769|
770|            if e.is_Integer:
771|                if e.is_positive:
772|                    rv = Mul(*nc*e)
773|                else:
774|                    rv = 1/Mul(*nc*-e)
775|                if cargs:
776|                    rv *= Mul(*cargs)**e
777|                return rv
778|
779|            if not cargs:
780|                return self.func(Mul(*nc), e, evaluate=False)
781|
782|            nc = [Mul(*nc)]
783|
784|        # sift the commutative bases
785|        sifted = sift(cargs, lambda x: x.is_real)
786|        maybe_real = sifted[True] + sifted[None]
787|        other = sifted[False]
788|        def pred(x):
789|            if x is S.ImaginaryUnit:
790|                return S.ImaginaryUnit
791|            polar = x.is_polar
792|            if polar:
793|                return True
794|            if polar is None:
795|                return fuzzy_bool(x.is_nonnegative)
796|        sifted = sift(maybe_real, pred)
797|        nonneg = sifted[True]
798|        other += sifted[None]
799|        neg = sifted[False]
800|        imag = sifted[S.ImaginaryUnit]
801|        if imag:
802|            I = S.ImaginaryUnit
803|            i = len(imag) % 4
804|            if i == 0:
805|                pass
806|            elif i == 1:
807|                other.append(I)
808|            elif i == 2:
809|                if neg:
810|                    nonn = -neg.pop()
811|                    if nonn is not S.One:
812|                        nonneg.append(nonn)
813|                else:
814|                    neg.append(S.NegativeOne)
815|            else:
816|                if neg:
817|                    nonn = -neg.pop()
818|                    if nonn is not S.One:
819|                        nonneg.append(nonn)
820|                else:
821|                    neg.append(S.NegativeOne)
822|                other.append(I)
823|            del imag
824|
825|        # bring out the bases that can be separated from the base
826|
827|        if force or e.is_integer:
828|            # treat all commutatives the same and put nc in other
829|            cargs = nonneg + neg + other
830|            other = nc
831|        else:
832|            # this is just like what is happening automatically, except
833|            # that now we are doing it for an arbitrary exponent for which
834|            # no automatic expansion is done
835|
836|            assert not e.is_Integer
837|
838|            # handle negatives by making them all positive and putting
839|            # the residual -1 in other
840|            if len(neg) > 1:
841|                o = S.One
842|                if not other and neg[0].is_Number:
843|                    o *= neg.pop(0)
844|                if len(neg) % 2:
845|                    o = -o
846|                for n in neg:
847|                    nonneg.append(-n)
848|                if o is not S.One:
849|                    other.append(o)
850|            elif neg and other:
851|                if neg[0].is_Number and neg[0] is not S.NegativeOne:
852|                    other.append(S.NegativeOne)
853|                    nonneg.append(-neg[0])
854|                else:
855|                    other.extend(neg)
856|            else:
857|                other.extend(neg)
858|            del neg
859|
860|            cargs = nonneg
861|            other += nc
862|
863|        rv = S.One
864|        if cargs:
865|            rv *= Mul(*[self.func(b, e, evaluate=False) for b in cargs])
866|        if other:
867|            rv *= self.func(Mul(*other), e, evaluate=False)
868|        return rv

870|    def _eval_expand_multinomial(self, **hints):
871|        """(a+b+..) ** n -> a**n + n*a**(n-1)*b + .., n is nonzero integer"""
872|
873|        base, exp = self.args
874|        result = self
875|
876|        if exp.is_Rational and exp.p > 0 and base.is_Add:
877|            if not exp.is_Integer:
878|                n = Integer(exp.p // exp.q)
879|
880|                if not n:
881|                    return result
882|                else:
883|                    radical, result = self.func(base, exp - n), []
884|
885|                    expanded_base_n = self.func(base, n)
886|                    if expanded_base_n.is_Pow:
887|                        expanded_base_n = \
888|                            expanded_base_n._eval_expand_multinomial()
889|                    for term in Add.make_args(expanded_base_n):
890|                        result.append(term*radical)
891|
892|                    return Add(*result)
893|
894|            n = int(exp)
895|
896|            if base.is_commutative:
897|                order_terms, other_terms = [], []
898|
899|                for b in base.args:
900|                    if b.is_Order:
901|                        order_terms.append(b)
902|                    else:
903|                        other_terms.append(b)
904|
905|                if order_terms:
906|                    # (f(x) + O(x^n))^m -> f(x)^m + m*f(x)^{m-1} *O(x^n)
907|                    f = Add(*other_terms)
908|                    o = Add(*order_terms)
909|
910|                    if n == 2:
911|                        return expand_multinomial(f**n, deep=False) + n*f*o
912|                    else:
913|                        g = expand_multinomial(f**(n - 1), deep=False)
914|                        return expand_mul(f*g, deep=False) + n*g*o
915|
916|                if base.is_number:
917|                    # Efficiently expand expressions of the form (a + b*I)**n
918|                    # where 'a' and 'b' are real numbers and 'n' is integer.
919|                    a, b = base.as_real_imag()
920|
921|                    if a.is_Rational and b.is_Rational:
922|                        if not a.is_Integer:

1212|    def _eval_nseries(self, x, n, logx):
1213|        # NOTE! This function is an important part of the gruntz algorithm
1214|        #       for computing limits. It has to return a generalized power
1215|        #       series with coefficients in C(log, log(x)). In more detail:
1216|        # It has to return an expression
1217|        #     c_0*x**e_0 + c_1*x**e_1 + ... (finitely many terms)
1218|        # where e_i are numbers (not necessarily integers) and c_i are
1219|        # expressions involving only numbers, the log function, and log(x).

1221|        b, e = self.args
1222|        if e.is_Integer:
1223|            if e > 0:
1224|                # positive integer powers are easy to expand, e.g.:
1225|                # sin(x)**4 = (x-x**3/3+...)**4 = ...

1227|                    logx=logx), e), deep=False)
1228|            elif e is S.NegativeOne:
1229|                # this is also easy to expand using the formula:
1230|                # 1/(1 + x) = 1 - x + x**2 - x**3 ...
1231|                # so we need to rewrite base to the form "1+x"
1232|
1233|                nuse = n
1234|                cf = 1
1235|
1236|                try:
1237|                    ord = b.as_leading_term(x)
1238|                    cf = Order(ord, x).getn()
1239|                    if cf and cf.is_Number:
1240|                        nuse = n + 2*ceiling(cf)
1241|                    else:
1242|                        cf = 1
1243|                except NotImplementedError:
1244|                    pass
1245|
1246|                b_orig, prefactor = b, O(1, x)
1247|                while prefactor.is_Order:
1248|                    nuse += 1
1249|                    b = b_orig._eval_nseries(x, n=nuse, logx=logx)
1250|                    prefactor = b.as_leading_term(x)
1251|
1252|                # express "rest" as: rest = 1 + k*x**l + ... + O(x**n)
1253|                rest = expand_mul((b - prefactor)/prefactor)
1254|
1255|                if rest.is_Order:
1256|                    return 1/prefactor + rest/prefactor + O(x**n, x)
1257|
1258|                k, l = rest.leadterm(x)
1259|                if l.is_Rational and l > 0:
1260|                    pass
1261|                elif l.is_number and l > 0:
1262|                    l = l.evalf()
1263|                elif l == 0:
1264|                    k = k.simplify()
1265|                    if k == 0:
1266|                        # if prefactor == w**4 + x**2*w**4 + 2*x*w**4, we need to
1267|                        # factor the w**4 out using collect:
1268|                        return 1/collect(prefactor, x)
1269|                    else:
1270|                        raise NotImplementedError()
1271|                else:
1272|                    raise NotImplementedError()
1273|
1274|                if cf < 0:
1275|                    cf = S.One/abs(cf)
1276|
1277|                try:
1278|                    dn = Order(1/prefactor, x).getn()
1279|                    if dn and dn < 0:
1280|                        pass

1282|                        dn = 0

1371|                # Try to correct nuse (= m) guess from:
1372|                # (lt + rest + O(x**m))**e =
1373|                # lt**e*(1 + rest/lt + O(x**m)/lt)**e =
1374|                # lt**e + ... + O(x**m)*lt**(e - 1) = ... + O(x**n)

1391|            if bs.is_Add:

108|    +--------------+---------+-----------------------------------------------+
109|    | expr         | value   | reason                                        |
110|    +==============+=========+===============================================+
111|    | z**0         | 1       | Although arguments over 0**0 exist, see [2].  |
112|    +--------------+---------+-----------------------------------------------+
113|    | z**1         | z       |                                               |
114|    +--------------+---------+-----------------------------------------------+
115|    | (-oo)**(-1)  | 0       |                                               |
116|    +--------------+---------+-----------------------------------------------+
117|    | (-1)**-1     | -1      |                                               |
118|    +--------------+---------+-----------------------------------------------+

121|    |              |         | where the base is assumed to be positive.     |
122|    +--------------+---------+-----------------------------------------------+
123|    | 1**-1        | 1       |                                               |
124|    +--------------+---------+-----------------------------------------------+
125|    | oo**-1       | 0       |                                               |
126|    +--------------+---------+-----------------------------------------------+
127|    | 0**oo        | 0       | Because for all complex numbers z near        |
128|    |              |         | 0, z**oo -> 0.                                |
129|    +--------------+---------+-----------------------------------------------+

132|    |              |         | values or rotating in the complex plane.      |
133|    |              |         | It is convenient, however, when the base      |
134|    |              |         | is positive.                                  |
135|    +--------------+---------+-----------------------------------------------+
136|    | 1**oo        | nan     | Because there are various cases where         |
137|    | 1**-oo       |         | lim(x(t),t)=1, lim(y(t),t)=oo (or -oo),       |
